Rafael Ojeda

José Rafael Ojeda Durán (born 3 February 1954) is the former Mexican Secretary of the Navy in the Cabinet of Andrés Manuel López Obrador. He has worked in the Mexican Navy in various positions for nearly 50 years. He is a member of the Mexican Legion of Honor.

José Rafael Ojeda Durán was born on 3 February 1954. Joining the Heroica Escuela Naval Militar (where he later served as a professor) in 1969, he later graduated as a Guardiamarina (Midshipman) in 1974. In the time after his graduation, he served in the Navy for 50 years on a variety of vessels, commands, and assorted offices. Among these: he led the Eighth Naval Region, Fourteenth Naval Region, Sixth Flotilla, Pacific Naval Force, Chief of Naval Operations, and was a Senior Naval Admiral. Durán was appointed to Secretariat of the Navy under the presidential cabinet of Andrés Manuel López Obrador, having prior served as an Inspector and General Comptroller of the Navy. He was appointed on 30 November 2018.

Durán was criticized for not investigating the Iguala mass kidnapping when it was theorized that the 43 victims were incinerated by sailors operating in the Eighth Naval Region, which he had control over at the time.

In 2020, he announced a so-called 'Naval Plan' to help aid those affected by Tropical Storm Hernan. This program consisted of rescue operations, cleanup, and evacuations, conducted by 450 units of the Mexican Navy.

Jean-Pierre Milovanoff

Jean-Pierre Milovanoff (born 1940, in Nîmes) is a French writer, laureate of several literary prizes Milovanoff's father was born in Russia and left his country in 1919; His mother is of Provencal origin. He studied letters at Montpellier and at the Sorbonne. He is a radio producer at France Culture and lived successively in Paris, Montpellier and Copenhagen. His first novel La Fête interrompue was published in 1970. He wrote three collections of poems entitled Borgo Babylone, La Ballade du lépreux et Noir devant. In 1997, Jean-Pierre Milovanoff received the prix Goncourt des lycéens for his novel le Maître des paons. He resides in Génolhac.

To: All Residents of Greenview Apartments 
From: Property Management Office 
Date: October 8, 2026 
Subject: Community Garden Use and Maintenance Guidelines

The community garden located behind Building C is an important shared space that offers residents the chance to grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers while fostering neighborhood connections. Starting this month, a formal schedule will be introduced to allocate plot assignments, watering duties, and seasonal clean-up responsibilities. All participants are asked to review the guidelines carefully and sign the attached acknowledgment form before beginning any planting activity.

Each gardening plot measures four feet by eight feet and is designated for a single household. Plots must remain within their assigned boundaries, and any expansion or modification of the garden beds requires prior approval from the management team. Compost bins are provided at the north corner of the garden; only organic kitchen waste may be deposited, and bins should be covered after each use to deter pests.

Watering is scheduled for twice daily during the summer months, with additional irrigation permitted during periods of drought as indicated by the local weather service. Residents are encouraged to use the rain barrels located near the east fence to conserve water and reduce reliance on the municipal supply. If a plot appears to be neglected for more than two weeks, the management office will contact the assigned household to discuss potential reassignment.

We ask all gardeners to observe proper hygiene and safety practices while working in the garden. Gloves, sturdy footwear, and sun protection are strongly recommended, especially when handling soil, pruning tools, or chemicals. The use of synthetic fertilizers or pesticides is prohibited; only approved organic alternatives may be applied, and any such products must be clearly labeled and stored in the designated supply shed.

The garden is a shared environment, and respectful behavior is essential to maintain its pleasant atmosphere. Noise levels should be kept low, especially after 9 p.m., and all tools must be returned to the tool rack after use. Children are welcome to assist with planting under adult supervision, but they must remain within the fenced area at all times.

Management will conduct a quarterly inspection to assess the overall health of the garden and address any concerns raised by participants. Feedback forms will be distributed during the next resident meeting, and suggestions for improvement are always appreciated. Thank you for your cooperation in keeping the community garden thriving and enjoyable for everyone.

Subject: Evaluating our next cloud storage provider
Hi Sarah,
I have been spending the last few days digging into our current storage costs and performance bottlenecks. As our data footprint grows, the premium we are paying for high-throughput tiers is starting to strain the quarterly budget. It is becoming clear that we need to restructure how we archive versus actively use our files, and I want to propose a shift to a more tiered multi-cloud approach before the next renewal cycle.
The immediate concern is no longer just raw capacity but egress fees and latency for remote teams. Our current provider charges significantly for data transfer, which hurts the productivity of the design team who constantly swap large video assets. I have found that splitting our active production data on a high-performance object store while moving our cold backups to a cheaper, archive-optimized service could reduce our monthly spend by nearly thirty percent without sacrificing accessibility for critical projects.
I also looked into security and compliance features, which were previously underutilized in our setup. The new configuration I am testing offers better version control and automated lifecycle policies that can tag and migrate files based on access frequency. This automation removes the manual overhead we currently face when cleaning up old project folders, ensuring we stay compliant with our data retention policies without requiring constant human intervention from the IT staff.
There is some initial work involved in migrating the existing dataset, which might cause minor disruption during the transition period. However, I have outlined a phased migration plan that allows us to move non-critical assets first. We can monitor the new environment for two weeks to ensure stability and speed before fully committing. I have attached a comparison spreadsheet that breaks down the projected savings and the specific tiered pricing models I am recommending for our review.
Let me know if you have time early next week to discuss this further. I would value your input on whether the proposed tiering strategy aligns with your long-term scalability goals. I am confident that optimizing this infrastructure now will save us significant resources in the coming year and give us the flexibility to expand our capabilities as the company grows.
Best regards,
Alex

Jordan Walne

Jordan Walne (born 28 December 1992) is an English professional rugby league footballer who plays in the second-row for the Barrow Raiders in the Championship. He has previously played for Hull Kingston Rovers and the Salford Red Devils in the Super League, plus Oldham RLFC on dual-registration.

He is the brother of fellow rugby league footballer, Adam Walne. As an amateur he played for the Leyland Warriors, based at Malt Kiln Fold, Leyland.

Tadao Watanabe

Tadao Watanabe (渡辺 忠雄, Watanabe Tadao; 15 July 1898 - 6 May 1980) was a Japanese politician who served as the Mayor of Hiroshima from 1955 to 1959. Watanabe was elected to the House of Representatives in April 1946, but soon after lost his seat due to the purge of Japanese officials by the US occupation authorities. He was able to return to political activity only following the end of the Allied occupation in 1952.

In April 1955 ran against Shinzo Hamai, and won the election after making allegations of financial misconduct by his opponent. As Mayor of Hiroshima, Watanabe was in favor of the exact reconstruction of the Hiroshima Castle, which was completed in 1958. In 1956, he inaugurated the statue of the goddess Kannon in the Peace Park in memory of those killed and in anticipation of peace. [1]. As mayor of Hiroshima, Watanabe supported the notion of establishing nuclear power plants in his city. Watanabe was survived by his son Naoyuki Watanabe, who worked to cultivate his father's legacy.

Watanabe tried to get reelected as mayor of Hiroshima in 1959, 1963 and 1967, but failed. After losing the election in 1959, Watanabe returned to his work as a lawyer. He died of uremia at Hiroshima Municipal Hospital at 2:35 p.m. (Japan time) on 6 May 1980.

Interview by Watanabe to the Los Angeles Times [2] Article in Time mentioning Watanabe [3] Norioki Ishimaru, Reconstruction planning after the Second World War in Hiroshima Archived 2012-02-08 at the Wayback Machine

Memo Number 2024-118. This communication serves as the official itinerary and logistical plan for the upcoming vendor negotiations in Chicago, scheduled for October 12 through October 15. All department heads involved in the account must review the attached flight confirmations and hotel reservations by the end of the business day on Monday to ensure compliance with the travel policy effective this quarter. The primary objective of this trip is to finalize the annual contract renewal with our largest distribution partner, thereby securing exclusive rights for the next fiscal year. Accordingly, all non-essential meetings have been deferred to allow adequate time for deep-dive analysis of their proposed fee structures and volume discounts, which require detailed financial modeling in real-time during the sessions.

Departure procedures are planned for the early morning of October 12 to maximize productive hours upon arrival. United Flight UA 342 departs from hub terminal B at 6:45 AM, arriving at O'Hare International Airport by 10:12 AM. Ground transportation has been pre-arranged with a chartered luxury van service to transport the delegation directly to the hotel, thereby eliminating the need for time-consuming individual taxi arrangements or reliance on local traffic congestion that is typically severe during weekday late mornings. The selected accommodation, the Hilton Loop, offers central access to the downtown financial district and is located within a ten-minute walk of the negotiation venue, ensuring punctuality and reducing the stress of daily commuting for the entire team.

The first two days will be dedicated exclusively to substantive discussions with the vendor's executive team. Day one focuses on reviewing current performance metrics and identifying areas where previous service levels fell short of contractual obligations, allowing us to leverage these points for better service guarantees. Day two is reserved for negotiating the pricing architecture, specifically targeting a tiered discount model that scales with projected volume increases over the coming eighteen months. Sales and procurement leads must prepare detailed scenario analyses beforehand to support their arguments with robust data, ensuring that every counter-offer is grounded in measurable projections rather than speculative assumptions.

On October 14, the schedule includes a half-day break to foster informal relationship building, followed by a working lunch with the legal teams to draft the final addenda clauses. The balance of the afternoon is allocated for internal debriefing among our representatives to align on next steps before concluding the day. A tentative dinner invitation from the client's senior leadership is expected, which should be accepted to demonstrate our commitment to long-term partnership beyond immediate transactional benefits. This social element is critical for understanding their internal dynamics and identifying potential allies who may support our position during final approval processes later in the quarter.

Return travel is scheduled for the end of business on October 15, with a late afternoon flight, UA 789, departing at 5:30 PM to allow for a buffer in case negotiations run longer than anticipated. All per diem expenses must be claimed using the new digital expense portal within forty-eight hours of returning to home base. No outstanding invoices or open action items should be carried over to the following week without explicit sign-off from the regional director. Failure to adhere to these guidelines will result in delayed reimbursement processing. Please direct any urgent inquiries regarding visa requirements or special dietary needs to the travel desk by October 1st to ensure all logistics are fully prepared.

Home | About | Contact

Kaptein started playing football at Achilles '12. Already at the age of 15, she received a professional contract with FC Twente Enschede. Capping off her first season with the league title, she also featured in the 2021/22 UEFA Champions League qualifying, scoring the goal in the opening game against FC Nike Tbilisi to make it 9-0. Twente, however, lost out to Benfica in the Champions Path final. A year later, Benfica was the last stop on the way to the group stage. In March 2023, Kaptein was voted one of the nine best talents in the world. Kaptein made her debut for Chelsea on 27 September, 2024. She scored her first goal for the club in the 5-0 win against Everton on 3 November.

Kaptein played some games for the Dutch junior teams from the U-15. With the U-17 team, she took part in the first and second qualifying rounds of the 2022 U-17 European Championship, which was successfully completed in April 2022, where she was captain in the second round. However, she was not part of the squad for the finals in May 2022, because she was wanted for the end of the league season. With the U-19 team, she qualified in October 2022 for the second qualifying round for the 2023 U-19 European Championship. She was not used in the second round in April 2023, as she was nominated for the senior national team games that took place at the same time. On 11 April 2023, she had her first senior cap. She came on as a substitute in the 81st minute for Lieke Martens in a friendly they won 4-1 against Poland. On 30 June 2023, she was nominated for the World Cup finals. She was the youngest World Cup debutant ever for the Dutch national team.

Erasmo Wong Lu

Erasmo Jesús Rolando Wong Lu Vega is a Peruvian civil engineer and businessman. He is the current owner of Willax Televisión and the Shopping Centers Lima Plaza Norte and Mall del Sur.

Erasmo Wong Lu, a Chinese Peruvian, was born in Lima in 1943. He was son of Erasmo Wong Chiang, a Chinese immigrant and entrepreneur and Angela Lu Vega, who owned a corner store-grocery and bazaar in the district of San Isidro in Lima. His father arrived in Peru at the age of eleven. As a child, Wong was kept busy with piano, accordion, shorthand and typing lessons. He lived in an apartment in the upper class San Isidro District, he helped his parents along with his brothers in the family store and attended the private school Colegio San Andrés. For his university education, Wong graduated with a civil engineering degree from Universidad Nacional de Ingenieria and earned postgraduate degrees in management from University of Piura.

Wong and his brother Edgardo established a poultry farm and tended it for seventeen years. In 1983 together with his father and brothers, and with the vision of being the best store in Lima, they founded the supermarket chain Wong, Eventually, Erasmo Wong Jr. became the head of his family's supermarket chain, also opening the supermarket chain Metro that then employed over 8,000 employees, advancing the company past Chilean competitors. Under the government of Alberto Fujimori, which surrounded itself with many Asian collaborators, spanning into the period of China's growing presence in Peru during the early 21st century, Wong began to approach Chinese entrepreneurs and the elite in Peru, establishing a higher social status in the process. In 1992 he was recognized as The Entrepreneur of the Year by IPAE - Instituto Peruano de Administración de Empresas. In December 2007, Wong supermarkets - which controlled sixty-two percent of Lima's grocery market at the time - was purchased from Wong's family by the Chilean retailer Cencosud for US$500 million. He still is a member of the Wong supermarket's board of directors. Since moving away from supermarkets, Wong has become the head of E W Corporation, which established many enterprises in the British Virgin Islands and Panama. In November 2015, Wong purchased Willax Televisión, a television channel that has since been described as promoting conservative and right-wing political stances by international media outlets. Perú.21 reported in 2019 that a group of Peruvian investors attempted to purchase the journalist branch of El Comercio Group in what was called "Operation Caledonia", with the operation reportedly receiving assistance of former mayor of New York City and Keiko Fujimori's former advisor, Rudy Giuliani. According to journalist Augusto Álvarez Rodrich, Wong was included in the Operation Caledonia group, Rafael López Aliaga and the Popular Force politician José Chlimper.

In 1999, Erasmo Wong Lu founded the Peruvian Chinese Association and its his currently President and also Director of its official magazine Integración. He lives in a home decorated with Chinese art. According to Look Lai and Tan, Wong had a net worth of US$500 million in 2010. He collects luxury cars, including various Porsche 911s, Ferraris, and a McLaren 720S. Politically, he has been involved in promoting rallies for right-wing politicians in Peru, especially for Keiko Fujimori and Rafael López Aliaga during the 2021 Peruvian general election. He also funded Fujimori's campaign for the 2011 Peruvian general election. Wong Lu signed the Madrid Charter, a document drafted by the far-right Spanish party Vox that describes left-wing groups as enemies of Ibero-America involved in a "criminal project" that are "under the umbrella of the Cuban regime".

.

Mafalda of Portugal

Infanta Mafalda of Portugal (c. 1195 - 1 May 1256 in Rio Tinto, Gondomar; Portuguese pronunciation: [mɐˈfaldɐ]) was a Portuguese infanta (princess) and later Queen consort of Castile for a brief period. She was the second youngest daughter of King Sancho I of Portugal and Dulce of Aragon. She became queen consort during her brief marriage to the 10-year-old Henry I of Castile. Upon the dissolution of the marriage, Mafalda returned to her homeland. She chose to become a Cistercian nun and became noted for the holiness of her life. She was beatified in the Catholic Church five centuries after her death.

Mafalda of Portugal was born around 1195, the daughter of King Sancho I of Portugal and his queen, Dulce of Aragon. On the death of her father, Mafalda, under the provisions of his will, was to receive the Seia Castle and the remaining portion of the municipality as well as all income produced there. Furthermore, she was granted the right to use the title of queen. This created a conflict with her brother Afonso II O Gordo, who, wanting centralized power, hindered his sister from receiving the titles and the corresponding rights. Afonso feared that something similar could happen with his two sisters, Teresa and Sancha, and their eventual heirs, creating a problem of sovereignty that could come to divide the country. Much of the Portuguese nobles sided with Mafalda and her sisters, but they were defeated. On the death of Afonso II, his son Sancho II granted some lands and castles to his aunts but he made them renounce the title of princess-queen. The final peace came in 1223.

In 1215, a political marriage was arranged between Mafalda and her young cousin Henry I of Castile. As he was about ten years old, the marriage was never consummated, and it was dissolved the following year on grounds of consanguinity. She then returned to Portugal.

In 1220, Mafalda chose not to marry again and became a nun at the Abbey of Arouca, though she was granted a special dispensation to retain control of her inheritance. Her sisters Sancha and Teresa also joined the convent. Mafalda later became abbess of the community, then one of Benedictine nuns, and in 1226 had her request to transfer the abbey to the Cistercian Order granted by the pope. Mafalda had a great devotion to Our Lady of Silva and made substantial donations to her shrine in Porto. She also had a hospice for travelers built as well as a number of bridges, churches, monasteries, and hospitals. She helped to establish her own abbey as a major religious center in the region, a status that endured for centuries. Returning from a pilgrimage to the shrine of Our Lady of Silva, she fell ill at Rio Tinto, Gondomar, and died at the monastery of Cistercians monks there on 1 May 1256. In 1616, wanting to return her body to Arouca as part of the process of her possible canonization, observers found her remains not to have deteriorated, which generated an even stronger public devotion to her. She was beatified in 1792 by Pope Pius VI. Her feast day is celebrated on 2 May.

Amish in Indiana

The state of Indiana is home to a large Amish population, estimated at 68,025 in 2026, the third-largest behind the states of Ohio and Pennsylvania. Around 1 in 7, or 16% of all Amish in the United States reside in Indiana. The largest numbers of Amish are primarily concentrated in the northeast of the state, however, smaller communities in the south also exist.

Adams County has the second-largest grouping of Amish in the state behind the Elkhart/LaGrange County region, with an estimated 11,055 adherents in 2025. The population in the county is primarily Swiss Amish. Amish settlement in the county began in the 1850s around the town of Berne.

Amish settlement in Allen County began in 1853, when a group of Amish families migrated to the area from Stark County, Ohio, and before that the area surrounding the town of Montbéliard in France. In 2020, Allen County had an Amish population of 4,577.

The combined Amish population in Elkhart and LaGrange counties in northern Indiana was 29,905 in 2025, making it the third-largest Amish settlement in the United States and the largest in Indiana. In 1986, roughly 75% of the farming population of LaGrange County was Old Order Amish. Due to their lifestyle, as well as their decision to not attend higher education, their high population has negatively affected the county's per-capita and educational attainment levels. As of 2020, LaGrange County was over one-third Amish. In 2002, Amish settlements in the two counties had an average of 139 members. Amish settlement in the region first began in 1841, after a group of four Amish began exploring land in the Midwest to establish a settlement. The group initially decided on land in Iowa, however while returning to their settlement in Pennsylvania they visited land near Goshen and decided to settle there instead. Four Amish families moved to the area the following year. At the time of their arrival, the Amish lifestyle did not differ significantly from that of their non-Amish counterparts in the county, with many non-Amish even speaking German. By the First World War, with the advent of new technologies, the Amish had become more of an ethnic enclave in the region. In 1874, the Illustrated Atlas of LaGrange County wrote of the Amish in the county as a "peculiar class of people... found mostly in Newbury and Eden.", and referred to them as "generally good farmers". In Newbury Township, the Amish owned nearly half of the real estate value and around 36 percent of "improved" land in the township. The Menno-Hof Amish & Mennonite Museum, a museum which displays the history of both groups, is located in Shipshewana, in LaGrange County.

In 1991, two Amish families moved from Lancaster County, Pennsylvania in Pennsylvania and began a settlement in Parke County, primarily due to overpopulation in Pennsylvania. In 2020, Parke County had a population of 1,351 Amish adherents.

In 2026, estimates from Elizabethtown College in Pennsylvania placed the Amish population in Indiana at 68,025, which accounted for .97% of the overall population, the highest percentage of any state in the country. In 2020, there were roughly 8.4 Amish for every 1,000 people in Indiana.

2002 Alabama Crimson Tide football team

The 2002 Alabama Crimson Tide football team represented the University of Alabama as a member of the Southeastern Conference (SEC) during 2002 NCAA Division I-A football season. Led by Dennis Franchione in his second and final season as head coach, the Crimson Tide compiled an overall record of 10-3 with a mark of 6-2 in conference play, placing first in the SEC's Western Division. However, Alabama was ineligible to compete in the 2002 SEC Championship Game or a bowl game due to a two-year postseason ban imposed as part of the penalty for National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) violations. The team played home games at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, and Legion Field in Birmingham, Alabama. Alabama began the season with a 4-1 record, only losing a close game at No. 8 Oklahoma. On October 5, the Crimson Tide lost another hard-fought game to the No. 4 Georgia, 27-25, at home. The team then defeated their next five opponents by an average of 24.4 points. In the Iron Bowl, Alabama lost to Auburn Tigers by a score of 17-7. The Crimson Tide ended their season with a win over Hawaii. On December 5, Franchione left Alabama to take the head football coaching job at Texas A&M University, which was left vacant by the firing of R. C. Slocum.

In the only game that Alabama would play at Legion Field in 2002, the Crimson Tide would score a season opening win for the first time since 1999.

The first road game of the year for Alabama would prove to be one of the most exciting game of the year. Despite trailing 23-3 at halftime, Alabama roared back in the second half with 24 unanswered points to take a 27-23 lead late into the 4th quarter. Oklahoma however, scored the last 14 points to win 37-27.

In the first game of the season at Bryant-Denny Stadium, The Crimson Tide would go over 500 yards of offense for the first time this season and win their first non-conference game at Bryant Denny Stadium since 1999. This game also was the first time since 1986 Alabama would not sellout their game at Bryant-Denny Stadium snapping a streak of 56 straight sellouts in Tuscaloosa.

For the second straight week, Alabama would hold their opponent to under 150 yards of total offense to win their third game of the season. This would be Ahmaad Galloway final game at Alabama as he would tear his ACL in the 4th quarter.

Shaud Williams would take the opening play 80 yards for a touchdown as the Crimson Tide beat Arkansas on the road for the first time since 1996.

For the first time since 1994, Alabama beat Tennessee snapping a seven year win streak that the Vols had. To date, this was the longest streak by any opponent over the Tide.

For the second year in a row, the Crimson Tide traveled to Vanderbilt and for the 18th straight time Alabama would beat Vanderbilt. This would be the last time Alabama would play Vanderbilt until 2006 snapping a 50 consecutive seasons streak of playing.

raw:
home internet plans

.

Choosing the right home internet plan is no longer just about streaming movies. With remote work, online schooling, and smart home devices becoming the norm, bandwidth demands have skyrocketed. Many households are finding that the entry-level packages from three years ago are insufficient for today's digital reality. Understanding your specific usage patterns is the first step toward avoiding frustration and extra costs.

Speed is often the headline feature, but it is not the whole story. Download speeds determine how quickly you can load content, while upload speeds matter critically for video calls, streaming, and cloud backups. A robust plan typically offers at least 250 to 500 Mbps to support multiple users simultaneously. If your household includes remote workers or gamers, you should prioritize higher upload limits and lower latency over raw download numbers.

Equally important is data caps. While many major providers have moved to unlimited tiers, some regional ISPs still enforce hard limits. Exceeding these caps can result in throttled speeds or overage fees. Always read the fine print to confirm if your plan is truly unlimited or if it allows for reasonable network management during peak hours. Transparency in these clauses saves you significant hassle later.

Consider the hardware you are using alongside your service. Most providers lease out modems and routers, which can add twenty to forty dollars per month to your bill. If you are comfortable setting up a personal network, buying a standalone router and a mesh system might offer better performance and long-term savings. Compatibility with your ISP's specific connection type, such as DOCSIS, is a crucial check before purchasing third-party gear.

Finally, review the contract terms and installation fees. Promotional rates usually expire after one or two years, leading to a significant jump in monthly costs. Auto-renewal clauses are common, so set a calendar reminder to reassess your needs annually. Switching providers is often easier than negotiating a rate increase, so keep your options open and stay informed about local alternatives.

Linpac

LINPAC Group Limited was founded in 1959 in Lincolnshire, England, as Lincolnshire Packaging - to produce paper packaging for local fresh food producers. It is now an international business valued at almost £500,000,000, providing mainly plastic packaging and supply chain manufacturing and services business. The company is based in Featherstone, West Yorkshire, England, and in 2015 had 2,500 employees worldwide.

LINPAC Packaging (formerly LINPAC Plastics), formed in 1969. LINPAC Allibert (created in 2007 from the merger of Allibert with LINPAC Materials Handling). Ropak Packaging (acquired in 1995). Viscount Plastics, acquired in 2001, was sold in 2012.

The company manufactures food packaging, returnable transit packaging (RTP), rigid plastic containers, cartridges, bulk storage tanks, bulk containers, medical containers, spill control products, and GRP gratings and structures. It also provides services related to these products - including design and manufacture - and asset management. LINPAC is a private company (ranked 37th in The Times Top Track 100 list of private UK companies 2010) and is owned by a consortium of banks. LINPAC's founders include Evan Cornish, who died in 2002. The Evan Cornish Foundation now supports, among other causes, the Louth & District Hospice. LINPAC's Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) code is 70100: Activities of head offices.

flood preparedness

Water moves fast when it is angry. It does not negotiate, and it does not wait for you to zip up your bag or double-check the map. Most people think they have weeks, but flash floods can transform a dry, sun-baked riverbed into a lethal torrent in under three hours. The first step in preparedness is not buying supplies; it is understanding that your safety plan must be automatic, not reactive. You cannot rely on a weather app notification when the cell service drops, so the knowledge of your local risk must be already in your head before the first cloud shadows the horizon.

Knowing where you stand is just as critical as knowing what is coming. Check your flood zone status through your local flood insurance map and look for physical markers on your property, such as flood lines painted on garage doors or the highest water marks on neighboring structures. If you live in a basement or on the first floor of a multi-story home, assume that water will reach you unless the ground slopes sharply away from the house. This assessment dictates where you place your valuables and where you store toxic supplies. You are not just preparing for a flood; you are preparing for the specific path water will take through your street, your neighborhood, and your home.

Inventory your documents and store them in a waterproof, fireproof container that is light enough to carry in a short burst of adrenaline. Bank statements, insurance policies, medical records, and digital backups are worthless if they are submerged in mud. Keep these items in a sealed bin placed on an upper shelf or in an attic, not in a bottom-drawer lock that will swell and jam when moisture hits the wood. Pair this physical security with a digital cloud backup updated monthly. If the power goes out, your passwords and contact lists need to be accessible on a device with a charged battery, not locked behind a dormant computer.

Your go-kit should be practical, not sentimental. Think of it as an extension of your body that allows you to survive seventy-two hours without standard utilities. Include a manual can opener, a battery-powered radio, non-perishable food that requires no cooking, and enough water to last three days per person. Add a flashlight with extra batteries, a multitool, and clean clothing suitable for wet conditions. Do not forget medications and special needs items for children, pets, or elderly family members. Test this kit annually; canned goods expire, batteries die, and medicines run out. A kit you forget about for two years is just a box of junk when the water rises.

Finally, map your evacuation route and practice it with your household, including children. Identify two different path options in case one is blocked by debris or stranded vehicles. Agree on a meeting place that is high ground, outside the immediate impact zone, and not reliant on cell phone communication. Know how to shut off the water, gas, and electricity in your home, and perform a dry run of this procedure once a year. These small, boring actions build the muscle memory that allows you to act decisively rather than freeze when the sirens begin to wail. Preparation is not about fearing the worst; it is about ensuring that when the worst arrives, you have already won the battle against chaos.

The purpose of this notice is to remind staff, patients, and families of the current visiting hour policy at St. Mercy General Hospital. Consistent visiting practices help maintain a therapeutic environment, protect patient privacy, and support the safe operation of clinical areas. Please read the following guidelines carefully and share them with anyone planning to visit a patient.

Visiting hours are scheduled from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily. During these times, a maximum of two adult visitors per patient is permitted, with each stay limited to one hour per visit. Children under the age of twelve may accompany an adult but must remain under supervision at all times. Visitors are asked to sign in at the main reception desk, present identification, and wear the visitor badge visibly while on the premises.

Exceptions to the standard schedule are made for intensive care units, neonatal services, and end-of-life care areas. In the ICU, visitation is allowed from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with a single family member permitted per patient and brief, frequent visits encouraged to reduce patient stress. For newborns in the NICU, parents may request 24-hour access after the initial 48-hour stabilization period, subject to staff approval. In hospice or palliative care settings, visiting hours are flexible and may be extended by the attending physician to accommodate family needs.

All visitors must observe hand- hygiene upon entry and exit, wear a mask in clinical zones, and refrain from bringing food, flowers, or gifts that could compromise infection control. Visitors are reminded to respect patient rest periods, keep noise to a minimum, and avoid lingering in hallways or waiting areas. Any behavior that disrupts care delivery or jeopardizes safety will result in a request to leave the facility.

The hospital security team and unit supervisors share responsibility for enforcing these guidelines. Questions or concerns regarding visiting policies should be directed to the Patient Services Office at extension 4321 or by email to visitinghours@stmercy.org. This policy will be reviewed annually and adjusted as needed to reflect best practices and evolving public health recommendations.

QSO B0738+313

QSO B0738+313 or B2 0738+313, is a quasar located in the constellation of Gemini. It has a redshift of (z) 0.630 and it was first discovered as an astronomical radio source in 1968 by astronomers who designated it as OI 363. The object has a radio spectrum appearing as flat making it a flat-spectrum radio quasar but also a gigahertz-peaked spectrum source.

QSO B0738+313 is classified as a core-dominated radio-loud quasar with an X-ray luminosity of L0.1-10 KeV ~ 45 erg s-1. However, the polarization level of the object is low. When observed by astronomers during R-band monitoring for four nights, its light curve was described as clear and almost sinusoidal with a few variations occurring on 21 January and 22 December 2006. In its spectrum, the quasar displays two dampened Lyman-alpha absorption-line systems located at redshifts of (z) 0.0912 and (z) 0.2212, making these the lowest known absorption-line systems of its kind. Two other faint companions were found, although not relating to the quasar. The quasar has a compact radio structure. When imaged with the Very Long Baseline Array at 15 GHz, it has two strong components. The first component is found weakly polarized at 0.5% with an inverted spectrum, while the other is polarized by around 1.5%. There are also weak and diffused radio lobes on each side of a much stronger radio component. Very Long Baseline Interferometry imaging at six centimeters showed the structure has an unresolved radio core, a small surface brightness radio emission surrounding the source and a jet located in north-south which extends by 5 milliarcseconds. This jet also displays a sharp bend at 45° towards the south-west direction with a knot at its bend.

An X-ray jet was discovered in QSO B0738+313 by Chandra X-ray observatory in March 2003. Based on results, the X-ray jet has an extent of 200 kiloparsecs and is narrow. Observations also showed the X-ray jet is curving as well, which then follows the path of a radio structure south of the quasar and terminating at a hotspot located within the southernmost part of a radio lobe. As it moves further from the core, the jet emission becomes fainter. Astronomers found the X-ray emission is centered strongly towards the jet's direction, 3.8 arcseconds south from the radio core suggesting location of innermost components of the jet.

Subject: Regarding the recent gear shift issues
Hi Sarah,
I finally got around to attempting the repair on the rear derailleur this afternoon. The shifting has been feeling really stiff lately, especially when climbing those steep hills near the park, so I knew it was time to take a look under the cogs. I spent the last two hours in the garage with the wheel removed, trying to identify exactly where the friction is coming from.
The chain appears to be in decent shape, so I did not think it was worn out just yet. I wiped down the derailleur hanger and checked for any bends or misalignments that might be causing the odd movement during the gear change. Everything looked relatively straight to the untrained eye, but the mechanism still felt sluggish when I spun the pedals against resistance.
I decided to remove the cage and clean out the accumulated dirt and grease from the pivots. It turns out there was a significant amount of grit packed into the tiny bolts that were binding the movement. After using the appropriate Allen keys and a drop of specialized lubricant on the joints, the cage swings much more freely now.
I reassembled the bike and took a quick test ride around the block. The shifting is noticeably smoother, although the top gear still requires a fine adjustment to the barrel adjuster. I will be completing that calibration tomorrow morning before the weather turns rainy again.
Let me know if you notice any persistent noises or issues when you next ride the machine. I will double-check the cable tension then as well to ensure we are good to go for the upcoming weekend trip. Thanks for your patience while I sort this out.
Best regards,
David

Effective immediately, Northbridge Community Bank is implementing a revised fee schedule for all domestic checking accounts. This update reflects significant changes in regulatory compliance costs, infrastructure maintenance, and the rising operational expenses associated with digital security services. The primary goal of this adjustment is to ensure the continued stability of our banking institution while maintaining the integrity of the services we provide to our valued customers. It is important to note that these changes were not made lightly and followed an extensive review period involving our financial operations team and external legal counsel to ensure full transparency with our client base.

The most notable change involves the monthly maintenance fee for Premier Checking accounts, which will increase from $10.00 to $15.00 per month. This specific tier includes advanced digital tools and dedicated customer support that carry higher associated costs. However, we are pleased to announce that the fee waiver threshold for this account type remains unchanged. Customers who maintain a direct deposit of at least $500.00 or a combined daily balance of $1,000.00 will continue to have this monthly charge waived entirely. We encourage you to review your current direct deposit setup to ensure you continue to qualify for this complimentary service without any interruption to your banking experience.

Regarding overdraft protection and insufficient funds, the standard overdraft fee will remain at $35.00 per item presented. We recognize that accidental overdrafts can happen to anyone, and we continue to offer the option to link a savings account or line of credit to prevent these fees. Additionally, the fee for returning a stopped payment request has been adjusted from $25.00 to $28.00 due to increased processing complexities. We advise clients to carefully verify payee details before submitting requests, as incorrect payments must be returned through a more labor-intensive manual process that contributes directly to the cost increase seen in this specific fee category.

Foreign currency exchange fees are also subject to update, with the spread on international transactions increasing by 0.5 percent. This modification aligns our rates with current market standards and helps offset the volatility risks inherent in cross-border transactions. Customers planning to travel outside the United States should be aware that ATM withdrawals made at out-of-network international machines will incur a surcharge of $5.00 in addition to the network operator's own fees. We remind all travelers to check with their destination banks in advance, as some institutions reimburse their clients for these surcharges, whereas others do not. Proactive planning can significantly reduce the financial impact of these global banking costs.

This updated fee schedule is available for download on our official website under the disclosures section and will be posted in all physical branch locations starting next Monday. Our customer service representatives have been trained on these changes and are available to discuss how they may affect your specific financial profile. We value the trust you have placed in us and remain committed to providing clear, honest, and fair banking services. If you have questions regarding your specific account status or fee waiver eligibility, please visit your nearest branch or call our dedicated support line during business hours. We appreciate your continued patronage and loyalty.

Guido Cappello

Born in Pisa, Guido Cappello moved to Gorizia at a young age, then in the 1960s to Milan. By profession he was an accountant. In the 1960s and 1970s Guido Cappello was one of the strongest Italian chess players. In 1960 he won the Italian Chess Championship in Perugia, ahead to Alberto Giustolisi, Federico Norcia and Enrico Paoli. Guido Cappello was awarded the title of National Chess Master in the same year. In the 1963 Italian Chess Championship in Imperia he still touched the title, ranking on equal points with the winner Ennio Contedini, who prevailed by technical play-off. Guido Cappello later achieved other excellent placings in this tournament: shared 3rd-5th place in 1965, 3rd place in 1967 and 1968, shared 2nd-4th place in 1972. Guido Cappello has had several successes in International Chess Tournaments, ranked 3rd in Savona (1967) and in Milan (1968). In 1964 he took part in the Baku International Chess tournament and scored 5,5 from 11. Guido Cappello played for Italy in the Chess Olympiads:

In 1966, at second board in the 17th Chess Olympiad in Havana (+10, =2, -6), In 1968, at second board in the 18th Chess Olympiad in Lugano (+5, =3, -7), In 1972, at first reserve board in the 20th Chess Olympiad in Skopje (+3, =5, -4), In 1974, at second reserve board in the 21st Chess Olympiad in Nice (+4, =3, -4). Guido Cappello played for Italy in the Clare Benedict Chess Cups:

In 1961, at first board in the 8th Clare Benedict Chess Cup in Neuhausen (+1, =0, -4), In 1964, at second board in the 11th Clare Benedict Chess Cup in Lenzerheide (+1, =1, -3). Guido Cappello was also a master of correspondence chess, achieving excellent placings in the ASIGC (Italian Association of Correspondence Chess) championships: 2nd place in the 15th championship, 4th place in the 18th, shared 4th-5th place in the 17th and 18th).

Boundless (video game)

Boundless is a massively multiplayer online sandbox game, developed by Guildford-based studio Wonderstruck Games. It was released through Early access on Steam for Microsoft Windows and OS X on November 13, 2014. It was fully released on September 11, 2018, and features online cross-play across all regions with PlayStation 4.

Played in either first-person or third-person perspective, players control a customisable avatar around procedurally generated planets, made up of various types and shapes of blocks. Players interact with these blocks and discover ancient technologies to help craft tools, weapons and machines which can then be used to shape the world around them into buildings, vast cities and guilds, and eventually allow players to open warps and portals to other worlds. Players are able to gather resources from their local environment, which are then used to survive and build equipment. Bases are built in the form of Beacons, which reserve an area for a particular player, protecting the land from being mined or otherwise edited by others. Players must also deal with hostile wildlife and survival matters such as hunger to survive in the alien universe of the game. Players are able to explore solo, or to play together in groups. Large groups of players collaborate to build intricate projects or undertake large-scale hunts.

In July 2014, the game was announced as a goal-funded project under the title of Oort Online. It quickly gained traction with its online audience as a browser-based game and reached its first funding goal in early August 2014. After quickly outgrowing the capabilities of the browser and the scope of the original game, it was decided that Oort Online would appeal to a wider audience under the Steam Greenlight system and was successfully greenlit in September 2014. Oort Online underwent a name change in October 2015 to the current title Boundless. Also in October 2015, it was announced that Boundless had been backed by Sony to be a console exclusive on their PlayStation 4 platform, allowing both PS4 and PC players to share the same online universe and play together. All planets in Boundless can be visited by using Portal technology, allowing players to step from one world to another in real time. As of September 11, 2022, after an extended development lull due to Wonderstruck assisting Larian Studios with Baldur's Gate 3, it was announced on the Boundless Forums that the development and rights to the game had been sold to the American Video Game developer Monumental, LLC, who would be taking over future updates and development of the game.

Boundless was developed and published by Wonderstruck. Boundless was released on Steam Early Access for Microsoft Windows and OS X on November 13, 2014. Boundless was released on PlayStation 4 on September 11, 2018, officially coming out of Early Access the same day on PC.

Harije

Harije is an elongated village on a hill ridge in the southeast part of the Brkini region along the road from Ilirska Bistrica to Podgrad. It lies at a watershed; springs flow to the south into Klivnik Creek and to the north into Posrtev Creek. Grmada Hill (516 m) stands east of the village and Ded Hill (576 m) to the west. Most of the cultivated land lies to the west and east, separated by meadows and pastures.

.

During the Second World War there was a Partisan checkpoint in the village. The Partisans operated a kitchen and had several bunkers in the village.

Harije is the site of four unmarked mass graves from the end of the Second World War. They all contain the remains of German soldiers from the 97th Corps that fell at the beginning of May 1945. The Cemetery Mass Grave (Slovene: Grobišče ob pokopališču) is located outside the north cemetery wall in the village. It contains the remains of four soldiers. The Vidos Oaks Mass Grave (Grobišče Vidosovi ceri), also known as the Mlake Lake Mass Grave (Grobišče pri jezeru v Mlakah), is located on the edge of the woods about 650 meters (2,130 ft) south of the village center and 40 m (131 ft) southeast of the main road. It contains the remains of four soldiers. The Laze Mass Grave (Grobišče Laze) lies next to the road, about 700 meters (2,300 ft) northeast of the village. It contains the remains of two or three soldiers. The Spring Creek Grave (Grobišče Studenčin potok), also known as the Studenčino Grave (Grobišče Studenčino), is located about 550 meters (1,800 ft) southwest of the main crossroads in the village. It contains the remains of one soldier.

Subject: Quick update on my training progress
Hi Sarah,
I wanted to drop you a quick note to share where I stand in my marathon preparation. It has been a challenging few weeks, but I am finally feeling a sense of rhythm in my long runs. The initial shock of increasing my mileage has settled, and I can genuinely say that the miles feel less like a punishment and more like a routine.
The past two weeks have been particularly intense. I pushed through a rough patch where my hamstrings were tight and my energy levels dropped sharply. I resisted the urge to cut corners, instead focusing on recovery dinners and extra sleep. It is a humbling reminder that consistency is far more important than any single heroic workout, especially when you are aiming for sustained output over twenty-six miles.
Right now, I am hitting forty-five minutes for every five miles on my midweek intervals. It is still below my target pace, but the trend line is definitely moving in the right direction. My Garmin data confirms that my heart rate variability is improving, which gives me confidence that my body is adapting well to the stress volume. I am taking it one zone at a time.
There is a mental component to all this that surprises me. In the first half of the training block, I was constantly thinking about the destination. Now, I have started to enjoy the middle miles of my long runs. There is a strange peace in outpacing the thoughts rather than letting them chase you down. I think that mental grit is just as critical as the physical conditioning for race day.
I aim to have a clearer picture of my pacing strategy by mid-October. Until then, I am staying disciplined with rest days, which feels counterintuitive but is undeniably effective. I appreciate your support and will keep you posted on how the upcoming tempo runs go. It is a long road, but I am enjoying the journey so far.
Best regards,
David

travel itinerary

Home | About | Contact

Planning a travel itinerary can feel like solving a puzzle, but the reward is a seamless journey that lets you soak up every highlight without the stress of last-minute scrambling. The first step is to define the purpose of your trip-whether it's a culinary tour of Tuscany, an adventure trek through Patagonia, or a relaxed beach escape in the Maldives. Knowing what you want to experience helps you allocate time wisely, set realistic travel distances, and avoid overloading your schedule with activities that clash.

Once your goals are clear, map out the major destinations and the order in which you'll visit them. A good rule of thumb is to limit the number of base cities to three or four, especially if you're traveling across time zones. This keeps travel time manageable and gives you a chance to explore each locale more deeply. Use a simple spreadsheet or a travel-planning app to list each city, the dates you'll arrive and depart, and the key attractions you want to see. When you spot gaps, consider adding a short day trip or a local market visit that can enrich the experience without demanding a full overnight stay.

Transportation logistics often make or break a trip, so research the most efficient ways to move between points. In Europe, high-speed trains can shave hours off a journey that would otherwise require a short flight, while in Southeast Asia a mix of buses and budget airlines can keep costs low. Book tickets in advance for popular routes, but leave room for flexibility by reserving a few "open" days where you can decide spontaneously based on weather or local recommendations. Don't forget to factor in airport transfers, check-in times, and potential delays; a well-timed buffer can save you from missing a connecting flight or a treasured sunset view.

Accommodations should align with both your itinerary and your budget. If you plan to spend several days in a single city, consider a central boutique hotel or an Airbnb that offers kitchen facilities, allowing you to unwind after long sightseeing days. For shorter stays, boutique hostels or guesthouses near transport hubs can be ideal, reducing the need for lengthy commutes. Always read recent reviews, check cancellation policies, and note any extra fees for amenities like Wi-Fi or breakfast, as these can add up quickly.

Finally, sprinkle in some local flavor by scheduling time for authentic experiences that aren't on the typical tourist radar. Book a cooking class with a local chef, join a guided walk through a historic neighborhood, or simply allocate an afternoon to wander a market and chat with vendors. These moments often become the most vivid memories of a trip. By balancing structured plans with pockets of spontaneity, you create a travel itinerary that feels both organized and alive, ensuring every mile traveled adds a story worth sharing when you return home.

They'll have to create a restaurant from the ground up with just $500 and six hours to feed 250 hungry guests! The bottom three earners will be up for elimination. | Ammerah, Kimmy | Patrick |
| 2 | Tantrum in Temecula | The Restaurant Express bus arrives in Temecula, Calif., a small, upscale town with lots of restaurants. The contestants' market knowledge is tested when they must propose to Robert and the mayor a new restaurant that they think could be successful in the town. The winner of the mini challenge will get extra money for the main challenge, where they will test their restaurant ideas on the locals at a lunch fair. The bottom three earners will be up for elimination. | Johnathan | Eric |
| 3 | Express: Impossible | The Restaurant Express bus arrives in Los Angeles, where the contestants face their first group challenge. Inspired by Restaurant: Impossible, the teams will be given 24 hours and $5,000 to revitalize two struggling restaurants. Robert and two visiting critics will dine at each location to determine who won this round, and who will be off the bus. | Bianca | None |
| 4 | Battle By the Beach | The Restaurant Express bus arrives at the iconic Balboa Pier in Newport Beach, Calif. The remaining five contestants will each have to open a concession stand with the same three dishes; a burger, a dessert and something on a stick. They also must produce a commercial for their stand. The contestant with the best commercial gets to have their ad play on the pier, but will that marketing advantage be enough to draw the most customers? | Patrick | Eric |
| 5 | Going, Going, Gone! | The remaining four contestants are given their biggest budget challenge: create a supper club with $1,000 and an empty restaurant shell. | 6 | The Truck Stops Here! | The three remaining chefs are each given a food truck and are challenged on their ability to serve specific groups of diners at three iconic locations: a zoo, an upscale shopping center and a late night bar scene. | 7 | Vegas or Bust | Jan and Seonkyoung battle to see who would face Adam in the final challenge. Seonkyoung won, therefore advancing herself to the final challenge. The two finalists then competed head-to-head against each other in the same restaurant. In the end, Seonkyoung beat Adam and she won a restaurant in the M, named Jade. | Jan, Adam | Seonkyoung |

newsletter roundup

A newsletter roundup is a curated collection of the most compelling stories, updates, and resources that have surfaced across a specific niche or industry over the past week or month. Rather than forcing readers to hunt through dozens of separate emails, the roundup delivers a single, easy-to-digest digest that highlights the best content, new product launches, upcoming events, and insightful commentary. For busy professionals, hobbyists, or casual fans, this format saves time, keeps them in the loop, and often surfaces hidden gems they might otherwise miss.

The appeal of a newsletter roundup lies in its ability to surface relevance without overwhelming the audience. Editors typically sift through a flood of submissions, social media chatter, and press releases, selecting only the pieces that add genuine value. By providing brief summaries and direct links, the roundup respects the reader's limited attention span while still offering enough context to decide what merits a deeper dive. This curation process also builds trust; subscribers come to rely on the editorial judgment that distinguishes noise from noteworthy.

From a business perspective, a well-executed roundup can boost engagement metrics and reinforce brand authority. When a company consistently delivers high-quality summaries, readers begin to view the newsletter as a go-to resource, increasing open rates and click-throughs. Moreover, featuring partner content or industry collaborators can nurture relationships and open doors for cross-promotion. The key is to maintain a balanced mix of original insights, external links, and occasional calls to action that feel natural rather than sales-driven.

Creating a successful newsletter roundup requires a few disciplined steps. First, set a clear scope: decide whether the focus will be broad, such as "tech trends this month," or hyper-specific, like "sustainable fashion startups in the U.S." Next, establish a reliable intake pipeline-monitor relevant RSS feeds, subscribe to niche newsletters, and track hashtags that signal emerging topics. Once the raw material is gathered, prioritize items based on originality, impact, and audience interest, then draft concise teasers that capture the essence without giving away the full story. Finally, schedule the send at a consistent cadence so readers know when to expect the roundup.

Readers often appreciate the added touch of community commentary. Including short quotes from experts, quick poll results, or user-generated questions can transform a static list into a lively conversation starter. Some newsletters even invite subscribers to submit their own picks, fostering a sense of ownership and encouraging deeper engagement. Over time, these interactive elements turn the roundup from a simple information dump into a vibrant hub where ideas circulate and relationships form.

In an age where inboxes are overflowing, the newsletter roundup stands out as a pragmatic solution for both content creators and consumers. By filtering the signal from the static, it delivers a focused, value-rich experience that keeps audiences informed, inspired, and ready to act. Whether you're a marketer looking to showcase industry highlights, a community leader aiming to amplify member contributions, or a reader craving a reliable digest, mastering the art of the roundup can transform the way you stay connected in a crowded digital world.

Merchant Ivory Productions

Merchant Ivory Productions is a film company founded in 1961 by producer Ismail Merchant (1936-2005) and director James Ivory (b. 1928). Merchant and Ivory were life and business partners from 1961 until Merchant's death in 2005. During their time together, they made 44 films. The films were for the most part produced by Merchant and directed by Ivory, and 23 of them were scripted by Ruth Prawer Jhabvala (1927-2013) in some capacity. The films were often based upon novels or short stories, particularly the work of Henry James, E. M. Forster, and Jhabvala herself. The initial goal of the company was "to make English-language films in India aimed at the international market". The style of Merchant Ivory films set and photographed in India became iconic. The company also went on to make films in the United Kingdom and America. Some actors and producers associated with Merchant Ivory include Maggie Smith, Leela Naidu, Madhur Jaffrey, Aparna Sen, Shashi Kapoor, Jennifer Kendal, Hugh Grant, James Wilby, Rupert Graves, Simon Callow, Anthony Hopkins, Glenn Close, Uma Thurman, Emma Thompson, Vanessa Redgrave, Natasha Richardson, Ralph Fiennes, Colin Firth, Richard Hawley and Helena Bonham Carter. Of this collaboration, Merchant once commented: "It is a strange marriage we have at Merchant Ivory... I am an Indian Muslim, Ruth is a German Jew, and Jim is a Protestant American. Someone once described us as a three-headed god. Maybe they should have called us a three-headed monster!" The expression "Merchant-Ivory film" has made its way into common parlance, to denote a particular genre of film rather than the actual production company. While 1965's Shakespeare Wallah put this genre on the international map, its heyday was the 1980s and 1990s with such films as A Room with a View (1985) and Howards End (1992). A typical "Merchant-Ivory film" would be a period piece, based on a classic novel, set in the early 20th century, usually in Edwardian England, featuring lavish sets and top British actors portraying genteel characters who suffer from disillusionment and tragic entanglements. The main theme often surrounded a house, which took on a particular importance in many Merchant Ivory films.

Merchant Ivory Productions was founded in 1961 by Ismail Merchant and James Ivory in India to produce English-language films. After early, modest successes with films such as The Householder, Shakespeare Wallah, and Bombay Talkie, Merchant and Ivory suffered a lean period during the 1970s. Films such as Jane Austen in Manhattan and The Wild Party failed to find an audience. Their fortunes revived dramatically in 1979 when they made an adaptation of Henry James' novel The Europeans. Their film Heat and Dust (1983) was an art-house hit in Europe, particularly in England. However, it was not until their work together on A Room with a View (1985) that they broke out from the art house into broader success. In 1985, Merchant Ivory Productions was signed by film distributor Cinecom International Films in order to give Cinecom access to the 11 Merchant Ivory productions at that time as Cinecom had to increase its distribution schedule. In 1986, Merchant Ivory and Cinecom began their co-production lineup with the film The Deceivers. In 1987, after 25 years as an independent producer, Merchant Ivory Productions declined offers by Hollywood power brokers and deep-pocketed investors, mesmerized by the success of the triple-Oscar winning A Room with a View, to take the company public. Around 1990, they moved their productions to England and the United States. Ruth Prawer Jhabvala became their frequent collaborating writer. Major film studios sought them out; Disney signed Merchant Ivory Productions to a three-year distribution deal in 1991. In October 2015, Cohen Media Group acquired the Merchant Ivory brand and library, 21 films and nine documentaries including worldwide distribution, for restoration and rerelease as a part of the Cohen Film Collection. Ivory would be creative director on the films' restoration, re-release and promotion.

Ivory was known for often directing the productions. He received three Academy Award nominations for his work but never won. He received his first Oscar at the age of 89 for his screenplay for Call Me by Your Name, becoming the oldest person to win an Oscar for writing. Academy Awards

Hawley started in 1987 as Ivory's first assistant director on Slaves of New York. He was involved in every project to some degree thereafter. In 1994, he started co-running the company with Merchant and departed in 2009 after completion of The City of Your Final Destination.

Subject: Updates on the spring planting and volunteer shifts
Hello neighbors,
I hope everyone is enjoying the mild weather this week. I am writing to share some important updates regarding our community garden as we prepare for the main spring planting season. The ground has finally dried out sufficiently after the heavy rains last month, which means we can begin turning the soil in the large north bed. This is a critical step that ensures our seedlings have a healthy, aerated environment to establish their roots. I want to remind everyone to check the tool shed for garden forks before you arrive, as we are doing a deep turn this year to help break up the compaction from last winter.
We have received a generous donation of organic compost from the local landscaping company, which has been delivered to the back corner of the plot. Please help out by spreading this material thinly over the tomato and pepper beds. The compost is rich in nitrogen, so it should give our early vegetables a strong start. If you are scheduled for the Saturday morning shift, please bring a pair of work gloves and a bucket. We aim to finish distributing the compost by ten in the morning so that afternoon volunteers can focus on laying out the irrigation lines.
On a related note, the water system repair is almost complete. The main valve leak that plagued us last summer has been fixed by the city services team. We will be testing the entire network on Thursday afternoon between one and three. There will be a temporary water outage in the garden area during this time, so please plan your personal schedules accordingly. It is a bit of an inconvenience, but long-term reliability is worth the short disruption. I appreciate your patience as we navigate these municipal service delays.
I also wanted to touch on the community potluck that was discussed at last month's board meeting. We have decided to move it to the third Saturday of June to coincide with the strawberry harvest. This change allows us to celebrate our first major yield of the season with a larger group. Volunteers are needed to set up tables, purchase basic supplies, and coordinate the food donation sign-up sheet. The sheet is located on the whiteboard inside the potting shed. Please mark your name down if you plan to bring a dish or sweet treat to share with the group.
Finally, please remember to water your assigned plots on a regular schedule, especially during the upcoming heat spells. Plants under stress are more susceptible to pests and disease, so consistent hydration is key to a successful harvest. If you are away from the city for more than a few days, kindly arrange for a neighbor to cover you or notify the plot coordinator so we can adjust the rotation. Thank you all for your continued dedication and hard work. It is truly a privilege to share this green space with such a supportive and energetic group of people. Let's make this season our best one yet.
Sincerely,
Elena Rodriguez
Garden Plot Coordinator

Subject: Understanding Open Source Licenses for Our Upcoming Project
Hi Alex,
I hope you're doing well. I wanted to take a moment to discuss the open source licenses we're likely to encounter as we evaluate components for the new platform. Choosing the right license is essential not only for legal compliance but also for maintaining the flexibility and community support that open source can provide. In the past, we've run into issues when a library's license conflicted with our internal policies, so it's worth revisiting the basics before we finalize any dependencies.
The most common licenses you'll see are the permissive ones, such as MIT, BSD, and Apache 2.0. These generally allow us to use, modify, and redistribute the code with minimal restrictions, often only requiring attribution. Apache 2.0 adds an explicit patent grant, which can be valuable if we're concerned about patent claims from contributors. On the other hand, copyleft licenses like GPLv3 require that any derivative work be released under the same license, which could compel us to open-source our own modifications. That's a significant consideration if we intend to keep certain parts of the platform proprietary.
We also need to be aware of LGPL, which sits somewhere in between. It permits linking to the library from proprietary software, provided that any changes to the library itself remain open source. This can be a good compromise when we want to benefit from a robust library without exposing our entire codebase. Additionally, some projects use dual licensing, offering both an open source and a commercial option, which could give us more flexibility if we later need a commercial support agreement.

raw:
dormitory rules

Moving into a dormitory marks one of the most significant independent living experiences for many college students. While the freedom is exhilarating, confusion often arises regarding the specific house rules that govern life within the halls. These regulations are not merely bureaucratic hurdles designed to make life difficult; they serve as the foundational framework that ensures safety, equity, and a livable environment for hundreds of individuals sharing limited resources. Understanding these expectations early on is crucial for avoiding petty conflicts and disciplinary action that can detract from the academic and social journey.

The most strictly enforced rules usually revolve around safety and fire prevention. Residential life staff are vigilant about blocking fire exits, using unregistered appliances, or smoking on campus. These are non-negotiable boundaries because they directly impact the physical well-being of the entire building. Students are required to keep hallways clear of clutter and ensure that their electrical setups do not pose a shock hazard. Ignoring these basic safety protocols can lead to immediate remediation costs or, in severe cases, removal from the housing contract. Compliance here is less about respect for authority and more about respecting the shared responsibility of keeping everyone out of harm's way.

Noise and guest policies form the second major pillar of dormitory living. Most institutions enforce quiet hours, typically from ten in the evening to seven in the morning, to accommodate early morning classes and different circadian rhythms. During these times, music, television, and loud conversations must be kept at a minimum. Guest rules are equally important, as they dictate who may enter the building, how long they can stay, and whether registration is required. Violating guest policies often gets worse than noise complaints, sometimes resulting in fines or contract termination, because it introduces security risks to the residential community. Failing to respect these temporal and social boundaries creates friction that is difficult to resolve once trust is broken.

Property and cleaning standards also play a vital role in maintaining a healthy living space. Students are responsible for the initial condition of their rooms and are expected to keep them free of mold, pests, and excessive clutter. The use of communal spaces like kitchens and lounges requires a reciprocal amount of cleanliness. Leaving dishes in shared sinks or trash accumulating in hallways is a common source of tension among residents. Most housing authorities conduct periodic inspections, and significant neglect can result in mandatory cleaning services billed directly to the student or their family. Maintaining these standards helps preserve the value of the housing and ensures a hygienic environment for all.

Finally, adherence to community guidelines regarding alcohol and substance use is heavily monitored. Many dormitories are dry, meaning no alcohol is permitted at any time, while others have designated social zones where consumption is allowed under strict supervision. Drugs and illegal substances are categorically forbidden. Enforcement of these rules is often handled discreetly by trained staff to address the issue while minimizing public embarrassment, but the consequence for violation is almost always severe. Ultimately, the goal of dormitory rules is not to police behavior but to create a predictable and safe container for personal growth and academic success. Respecting these norms demonstrates maturity and contributes to a positive living atmosphere.

Frontenac Secondary School

Frontenac Secondary School is a high school in the west end of Kingston, Ontario, Canada. The Limestone District School Board operates it. The team plays under the nickname "Frontenac Falcons".

Frontenac Secondary School was founded in 1957 as Collins Bay High School and adopted its current name in 1964. In 2006, construction began on a major extension, which includes a new library, a media room, an elevator, and several additional computer labs and classrooms.

Frontenac has junior and senior teams that compete in the Canadian game show Reach for the Top. In 1998-99, the senior team was the national champion. The team had qualified for the American game show Whiz Quiz. In 2007 and 2008, the senior REACH team was the international Whiz Quiz champions, and in 2006, 2007, and 2025 they attended the provincial REACH Championships.

Rob Bagg, former CFL player Wayne Cashman, former NHL ice hockey player and head coach. Taylor Hall, NHL hockey player and number 1 draft pick in the 2010 NHL entry draft Dee Sterling, former CFL player John Tripp, professional ice hockey coach and former player. Dylan Wykes, long-distance runner, qualified for the marathon in the 2012 Summer Olympics in London. Rick Smith, retired professional hockey player for the Boston Bruins Amanda Leveille, former professional hockey player, two-time Isobel Cup champion, and NWHL all-time record holder in wins Aaliyah Edwards, WNBA basketball player

raw:
Léman Manhattan Preparatory School

Léman Manhattan Preparatory School is a private school located in the Financial District, Manhattan. Students are ages two years old through eighteen years old. There are two Lower Manhattan sites. Founded in 2005 as Claremont Preparatory, the school was acquired by the Meritas family of schools in 2011, and subsequently renamed to Léman Manhattan Preparatory School. Several Meritas schools such as Collège du Léman which locates in Switzerland and Léman International School Chengdu which locates in China have incorporated the name Léman. In 2011, Léman joined Meritas, an international network of college preparatory schools. In 2015, Léman Manhattan was left out of a transaction that took in Léman Switzerland, and Léman Chengdu, and did not become an affiliate school of Nord Anglia Education as part of an acquisition deal. Nord Anglia currently maintains two other schools in Manhattan, Nord Anglia International School New York (ages 2-14) and the other school Avenues New York (ages 1-18) neither of which have an on site boarding facility. Léman Manhattan Preparatory School has students from over seventy countries. Tuition for K-12 day students and the boarding tuition is listed on their website.

Léman Manhattan's lower school is based at the former headquarters of Bank of America International at 41 Broad Street in the Financial District of Manhattan, New York City. and was the original campus. The middle and high school campuses are located nearby in the Cunard Building at 1 Morris Street, and opened in 2010. Both locations have amenities including swimming pools, art studios, libraries, gyms, music rooms, cafeterias and fine arts performing spaces. The lower school has a rooftop playground.

Léman Manhattan is the only high school in New York City with a residential boarding program. In 2012, the school opened its boarding program, with forty students from nine countries in grades 9-12 in its inaugural program. In 2015, Léman had over 100 students participating in its boarding program. Student housing is located at 37 Wall Street, an apartment building blocks away from the Upper School Campus. Students in the boarding program reside in apartments, with rooms accommodating 2-4 people with a kitchen.
