Date: 8 October 2026 
To: All Facilities Management Staff 
From: Director of Sustainable Operations 
Subject: Guidelines for Installation and Maintenance of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations

The purpose of this memo is to outline the standardized procedures for installing, operating, and maintaining electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure across all company sites. As our fleet expands and employee demand for charging options grows, it is essential that each location follows the same safety, accessibility, and performance criteria to ensure reliable service and compliance with local regulations.

All new installations must use Level 2 AC chargers rated at 7.2 kW minimum, equipped with SAE J1772 connectors and integrated network management software. Prior to any electrical work, the site's electrical engineer should confirm that the existing service panel can accommodate the additional load, and a load analysis report must be submitted to the Energy Compliance Team. Where possible, chargers should be positioned in well-lit, weather-protected areas within 5 meters of the nearest accessible parking space, and clear signage must be installed indicating the location and operating hours.

Routine maintenance will be performed on a quarterly basis by the contracted service provider. The maintenance checklist includes inspection of cable integrity, verification of ground fault protection, firmware updates, and cleaning of the charging enclosure. Any identified deficiencies must be recorded in the asset management system within 24 hours, and corrective actions should be completed no later than the next scheduled maintenance window unless an immediate safety risk is present.

User access will be managed through the corporate EV charging app, which assigns a unique ID to each employee and logs session data for billing and analytics. Employees are required to report any malfunction or unauthorized use to Facilities Management via the designated ticketing portal. Failure to follow proper charging etiquette, such as leaving a vehicle connected after charging is complete, may result in temporary suspension of charging privileges.

The implementation of these guidelines will support our sustainability goals, reduce operational disruptions, and provide a consistent charging experience for all staff. Please review the attached technical specifications and ensure that all upcoming projects incorporate these requirements. If you have any questions, contact the Sustainable Operations office directly.

raw:
garden pest control

Keeping your garden healthy requires a proactive approach to pest management. Many homeowners wait until plants are visibly damaged before acting, but early detection makes all the difference. Each morning, take a few minutes to inspect the undersides of leaves and stem junctions. Look for sticky residue, small holes, or clusters of insects. Catching an infestation early prevents it from spreading to other healthy specimens in your yard.

Before reaching for chemical sprays, consider introducing natural predators. Ladybugs are excellent at controlling aphids, while lacewants help manage whiteflies. You can also keep chickens or Ducks in secure areas of the garden if space permits. These animals naturally reduce the population of slugs, snails, and larger beetles that might otherwise chew through your tender seedlings. This biological method is cost-effective and maintains the ecological balance of your soil.

Physical barriers are surprisingly effective against common garden nuisances. Floating row covers protect brassicas from cabbage moths, while copper tape around raised beds deters slugs and snails. mesh bags work well for protecting berries from birds and fruit flies. These simple tools provide a defense mechanism that does not involve any synthetic chemicals, ensuring your harvest remains safe for consumption.

If pests persist despite these efforts, targeted organic remedies are the next step. Neem oil disrupts the life cycle of many soft-bodied insects without harming beneficial pollinators. Insecticidal soap works best on aphids and spider mites when applied directly to the foliage. Always follow label instructions carefully and apply treatments during cool parts of the day to minimize stress on your plants and maximize effectiveness.

Finally, focus on prevention by maintaining strong plant health. Weak plants are more susceptible to pest attacks, so ensure your soil is rich in nutrients and properly irrigated. Remove plant debris at the end of each season, as this eliminates overwintering sites for harmful insects. A tidy garden with resistant plant varieties provides the best long-term strategy for keeping pests under control.

Subject: Q2 2024 Sales Summary
Hi Team,
I'm pleased to share the quarterly sales summary for the second quarter of 2024. Overall, we closed the period with $12.4 million in net revenue, representing a 7.2 percent increase over Q1 and a 3.8 percent rise compared with the same quarter last year. The growth was driven primarily by strong performance in our enterprise software line and a notable uptick in new customer acquisitions across the Midwest region.
The enterprise software division posted $6.8 million in sales, up 11 percent from the previous quarter. This was largely thanks to the successful rollout of the latest version of our analytics platform, which has resonated well with larger clients seeking integrated data solutions. Our renewal rate for existing contracts held steady at 92 percent, indicating solid customer satisfaction and a healthy pipeline for the upcoming quarter.
Mid-market hardware sales saw a modest decline, slipping 2.3 percent to $2.1 million. While the dip is partially attributable to inventory constraints we faced in April, the team managed to offset some of the loss through aggressive promotional pricing in May and June. Looking ahead, the supply chain team has confirmed that the anticipated shipment arrivals next month should restore inventory levels, allowing us to meet the forecasted demand for Q3.
On the geographic front, the Midwest region delivered an impressive 15 percent increase in new business, contributing an additional $1.9 million in revenue. In contrast, the West Coast market remained flat, with sales holding at $2.3 million. The regional managers have identified several upcoming trade shows and partnership opportunities that we expect will reignite growth in the western market during the next quarter.
Finally, I want to acknowledge the cross-functional collaboration that made these results possible. The sales, product, and support teams all played a critical role in ensuring smooth onboarding for new clients and maintaining high renewal rates. Your dedication to meeting targets and addressing client needs does not go unnoticed, and it sets a strong foundation for continued success.
Please review the attached detailed report when you have a moment, and feel free to reach out with any questions or suggestions for improvement. I look forward to discussing our strategy for the next quarter at the upcoming all-hands meeting.
Best regards,
Laura Martinez
Senior Director of Sales
TechNova Solutions, Inc.

raw:
travel itinerary

When you open your laptop to plan a trip to an unfamiliar city, the screen often fills with a chaotic grid of pins, links, and nested spreadsheets. The temptation to over-pack the day is strong, driven by the fear of missing out on major landmarks or hidden gem cafes. However, the most memorable journeys rarely follow a rigid, minute-by-minute schedule. Instead, they emerge from a balance of structured anchors and flexible pockets of time. A realistic itinerary is not just a list of places to visit; it is a response to the natural rhythms of travel, accounting for fatigue, unexpected weather, and the simple joy of serendipity.

Start by selecting three non-negotiable activities for each day. These are your anchors, the experiences that define the location, such as a museum entry, a guided tour of the historic center, or a reservation at a highly-rated restaurant. Once these are locked in, group them geographically to minimize transit time. Shuttling across the city in traffic or crowded subways can drain the energy needed to actually enjoy the sights. By clustering activities within a specific neighborhood, you allow yourself to walk between destinations. This approach often reveals secondary beauties that cars or public transport would have allowed you to miss, turning a commute into a discovery.

Build in significant buffer zones, which are essential for the reality of travel. A two-hour delay in a flight, a sudden rainstorm, or a sold-out ticket can dismantle a tight schedule in seconds. Designate afternoons as low-commitment blocks where the only obligation is to rest, grab coffee, or wander aimlessly. This flexibility prevents the stress of racing between appointments. If you find that the line at a popular attraction is too long, you have the luxury to pivot without feeling like you have failed your own plan. Spontaneity is a feature, not a bug, in a well-designed trip.

Consider the physical toll of travel when assigning specific tasks to certain times of day. Early mornings offer quieter streets and better light for photography, making them ideal for active sightseeing. Late afternoons are often the best time to explore local markets or parks as the sun begins to set, creating a more relaxed atmosphere. Save heavy indoor museums or long walking tours for mid-morning or early afternoon when energy levels are generally higher, but temperatures and light conditions are moderate. Aligning your physical capabilities with the itinerary ensures that you finish the day feeling energized rather than exhausted.

Finally, write the plan down in a simple, portable format. While digital tools are convenient, they can be distracting and require battery power. A concise outline stored on your phone or printed on paper provides a clear reference without the clutter of endless tabs. As you travel, review this list the night before to confirm logistics, but keep the actual experience open to adaptation. The goal is not to check every box, but to ensure that your primary interests are honored while leaving room for the unexpected stories that only travel can provide. A realistic itinerary respects your presence in the moment, allowing the destination to unfold at its own pace rather than forcing it to fit into a rigid framework.

Prehistoric Rock-Art Site of Pala Pinta

The Prehistoric Rock-Art Site Pala Pinta (Portuguese: Abrigo rupestre da Pala Pinta) is a Paleolithic-era rock-art site, recognized for cave paintings in the Portuguese municipality of Alijó, in the civil parish of Carlão e Amieiro.

The cave was occupied during the 3rd millennium, and the rock art paintings were likely created during this period. After its discovery, on 30 December 1985, there was a move by the Serviço Regional de Arqueologia da Zona Norte (North Zone Regional Archaeological Service) to have the site classified for protection. There was a positive reaction on 21 April 1986 to the endeavour by the Consultative Council of IPPC. Further initiatives were undertaken on 7 May by the Secretária de Estado da Cultura (Secretary-of-State for Culture) to classify the archaeological site as a National Monument. Although this was never promulgated, on 18 July 2006, the area was defined as a Zona Especial de Classificação (Special Classification Zone) by the DRPorto.

It was situated in an isolated, rural area in the middle of the hilltop facing the east. The site includes rock-art paintings over granite surface, covering an area of 12 metres (39 ft) long and 2.50 metres (8.2 ft) high. There roughly two vertical panels, caused by fractures in the cave/clifftop, consisting of monochromatic paintings in ochre of radial imagery (likely sun or stars), points and anthropomorphic representations of figures.

Mesquita, Horácio de; Correia, Virgílio (1922), "Arte rupestre em Portugal - A Pala Pinta", Terra Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon, Portugal, pp. 145-147{{citation}}: CS1 maint: location missing publisher (link) Junior, Joaquim Rodrigues dos Santos (1933), "O abrigo pré-histórico da Pala Pinta", Trabalhos de Antropologia e Etnologia (in Portuguese), Porto, Portugal, pp. 33-43{{citation}}: CS1 maint: location missing publisher (link) Sousa, Orlando (1989), "O Abrigo de Arte Rupestre da Pala Pinta - Alijó", Trabalhos de Antropologia e Etnologia (in Portuguese), Porto, Portugal, pp. 191-198{{citation}}: CS1 maint: location missing publisher (link)

Steve Greer

Steve Greer (July 23, 1947 - December 13, 2021) was a college football position coach and executive between 1971 and 2009. During his playing career in the 1960s, he was the AA Lineman of the Year twice while at Greer High School and received All-America selections while at the University of Georgia. After briefly playing with the Toronto Argonauts in 1970, he started coaching the defensive line freshmen with the University of Georgia the following year. He continued his freshmen coaching experience with the offensive and defensive players at Auburn University until 1973. After moving to varsity football in 1974, he primarily continued his defensive coaching career with both universities until 1993. During this time period, Greer was the recruiting coordinator and defensive end coach with Georgia from 1979 to 1981. After starting an administrative assistant role with Georgia in 1993, he resumed his recruiting coordinator position in 1994. Three years later, he became the Director of Football Operations. He remained in the role until he decided to leave the university in 2009. After his football tenure, Greer was with Jim Whitehead Tire Service during 2011. Greer joined the South Carolina Football Hall of Fame in 2019.

Greer's birth occurred in Greer, South Carolina during July 23, 1947. During his childhood, he was a fruit packer and hunter. He began playing football at Greer High School in 1961. With the team, Greer played in the 1963 Upstate Class AA championship. That year, he was All-Southern and won the AA Lineman of the Year award. During 1964, he was named "outstanding lineman" after his South Carolina team won the Shrine Bowl of the Carolinas. For that season, Greer was All-Southern and the AA Lineman of the Year. At the 1965 North-South All-Star, he was Outstanding Lineman and won with the North. That year, Greer was on the freshman football team for the University of Georgia. He did not play in 1966 after knee surgery. Following his return to the team in 1967, Greer played at that year's Liberty Bowl. Additional bowl game appearances with Georgia were at the Sugar Bowl and Sun Bowl during 1969. That year, he became their captain. With the South, his team won the American Bowl and Hula Bowl in 1970.

In May 1970, Greer joined the Toronto Argonauts. He played on the team during July 1970 before being cut that month. In 1971, he was hired as a graduate assistant with Georgia. While there, Greer began his defensive line coaching career in freshman football. With his freshmen experience at Auburn University from 1972 to 1973, Greer was an offensive coach for one year and defensive coach for two years. Greer continued working as a defensive coach after moving to Auburn's varsity football team in 1974. He remained in his position with the university until he became the recruiting coordinator at Georgia during 1979. With Georgia, he was also a defensive end coach before ending both positions in 1981. Greer resumed his defensive line experience with Georgia that year. He remained there as their coach until 1993. Greer started his administrative assistant role in 1993. While in his position, he had become the recruiting coordinator by 1994. In 1997, Greer became the Director of Football Operations and left as coordinator. He remained as Director of Football Operations until he decided to leave Georgia in 2009. Outside of football, Greer was with Jim Whitehead Tire Service during 2011.

While at Georgia, Greer was All-Southeastern Conference for United Press International and The Associated Press in 1969. For All-America selections, Greer was chosen in 1968 by the Central Press. The following year, he was All-America for Central Press and The Associated Press. Greer received the Lineman of the Year award from the Atlanta Touchdown Club during 1970. During 2014, he joined the Georgia Bulldogs Circle of Honor. He became part of the South Carolina Football Hall of Fame in 2019.

During the late 2010s, Greer began experiencing amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in his arms. He had three children during his marriage. Greer's death occurred in Athens, Georgia on December 13, 2021.

2019 StarCraft II World Championship Series

The 2019 StarCraft II World Championship Series (WCS) was the 2019 edition of the StarCraft II World Championship Series, the top esports tournament circuit for StarCraft II. The tournament series' Global Finals were won by South Korean professional player Park "Dark" Ryung Woo.

The 2019 StarCraft II World Championship Series was separated into two regions, WCS Korea and WCS Circuit. The format of the former remained consistent with the standard set in 2017, featuring three seasons of the long-running Global StarCraft II League (GSL) Code S with two smaller GSL Super Tournament events interspersed. The format of the latter region, however, replaced one of the standard four large WCS Circuit events with WCS Winter, separated into WCS Winter Europe and WCS Winter America, two smaller tournaments with an online portion and an in-person playoff portion. Beyond this, the format remained unchanged, with three large WCS Circuit events and accompanying qualifiers under the WCS Challenger branding. Two shared World Championship Series Global events featured players from both regions before the Global Finals. All these events, excluding the second WCS Global event, GSL vs. the World, gave out WCS Circuit and/or WCS Korea points that determined the seeding of the Global Finals.

Eight players from each WCS region qualify for the event based on their WCS points-based rankings. Winners of WCS Circuit stops, GSL Code S events, and IEM Katowice receive automatic qualification. Based on their region-specific ranking, the sixteen players are then seeded into four four-player groups for the first round. A draw is held for the quarterfinals bracket, with winners of each group facing second-place finishers of other groups.

The WCS Global Finals were held at the Anaheim Convention Center in Anaheim, California, as part of BlizzCon 2019. They featured a group stage as the first round of play, played out the week before the main event, followed by bracket play from the quarterfinals onward at the convention center. For the first time ever, the event was confined to one of the two days the convention ran for, with all matches from the quarterfinals through the finals happening on November 1, Friday.

raw:
Chip art

Chip art, also known as silicon art, chip graffiti or silicon doodling, refers to microscopic artwork built into integrated circuits, also called chips or ICs. Since ICs are printed by photolithography, not constructed a component at a time, there is no additional cost to include features in otherwise unused space on the chip. Designers have used this freedom to put all sorts of artwork on the chips themselves, from designers' simple initials to rather complex drawings. Given the small size of chips, these figures cannot be seen without a microscope. Chip graffiti is sometimes called the hardware version of software easter eggs. Prior to 1984, these doodles also served a practical purpose. If a competitor produced a similar chip, and examination showed it contained the same doodles, then this was strong evidence that the design was copied (a copyright violation) and not independently derived. A 1984 revision of the US copyright law (the Semiconductor Chip Protection Act of 1984) made all chip masks automatically copyrighted, with exclusive rights to the creator, and similar rules apply in most other countries that manufacture ICs. Since an exact copy is now automatically a copyright violation, the doodles no longer serve a useful purpose in terms of hardware watermarking.

Integrated circuits (ICs) are constructed from multiple layers of material, typically silicon, silicon dioxide (glass), and aluminum. The composition and thickness of these layers give them their distinctive color and appearance. These elements created an irresistible palette for IC design and layout engineers. The creative process involved in the design of these chips, a strong sense of pride in their work, and an artistic temperament combined compel people to want to mark their work as their own. It is very common to find initials, or groups of initials on chips. This is the design engineer's way of "signing" their work. Often this creative artist's instinct extends to the inclusion of small pictures or icons. These may be images of significance to the designers, comments related to the chip's function, inside jokes, or even satirical references. Because of the difficulty in verifying their existence, chip art has also been the subject of online hoaxes (e.g. the never-seen "bill sux" comment on a Pentium chip-the reputed "photo" showing the inscription is a hoax). The mass production of these works of art on the body of a commercial IC goes unnoticed by most observers and is discouraged by semiconductor corporations, primarily from the fear that the presence of the artwork (which is clearly unneeded) may interfere with some necessary function or design flow in the chip. Some laboratories have started collaborating with artists or directly producing books and exhibits with the micrographs of these chips. Such is the case of Harvard chemist George Whitesides, who collaborated with photographer Felice Frankel to publish On the Surface of Things, a photography book on experiments mostly from the Whitesides lab. Also, the laboratory of Albert Folch (who, perhaps not coincidentally, works in BioMEMS, the same field as George Whitesides) at the University of Washington's Bioengineering Dept. has produced an online gallery with more than 1,700 free BioMEMS-related chip art micrographs and three art exhibits in the Seattle area.

The Silicon Zoo - A portion of the Molecular Expressions web site from Florida State University, containing pictures of hundreds of discovered chip artworks. The buffalo shown here is from this website.

Yahoo directory of chip art pages and articles. Chipworks An entire silicon art gallery found on the chips analysed by Chipworks. Chip graffiti from the Smithsonian Museum of American History Art on the Head of a Microchip, Bruce Headlam, New York Times, 4 March 1999.

Chip art, also known as silicon art, chip graffiti or silicon doodling, refers to microscopic artwork built into integrated circuits, also called chips or ICs. Since ICs are printed by photolithography, not constructed a component at a time, there is no additional cost to include features in otherwise unused space on the chip. Designers have used this freedom to put all sorts of artwork on the chips themselves, from designers' simple initials to rather complex drawings. Given the small size of chips, these figures cannot be seen without a microscope. Chip graffiti is sometimes called the hardware version of software easter eggs. Prior to 1984, these doodles also served a practical purpose. If a competitor produced a similar chip, and examination showed it contained the same doodles, then this was strong evidence that the design was copied (a copyright violation) and not independently derived. A 1984 revision of the US copyright law (the Semiconductor Chip Protection Act of 1984) made all chip masks automatically copyrighted, with exclusive rights to the creator, and similar rules apply in most other countries that manufacture ICs. Since an exact copy is now automatically a copyright violation, the doodles no longer serve a useful purpose in terms of hardware watermarking.

Gottfried von Erdmannsdorff

Gottfried von Erdmannsdorff (25 April 1893 - 30 January 1946) was a German general during World War II. He was convicted by a Soviet military tribunal for war crimes at the Minsk Trial and executed in 1946.

On 27 June 1944, as part of Mogilev Offensive, Soviet troops made a deep breakthrough north of Mogilev by crossing the Dnieper River over a bridge at Trebuchi. The 4th Army dispatched a message to Erdmannsdorff that Mogilev be held as a "fortified position" and ordered him to hold the town until the very last man. The 4th Army retreated the XXXIX Panzer Corps and the XII Army Corps a full 21km west of Mogilev, leaving the town to its fate against the overwhelming Soviet attacks. Later in the evening Erdmannsdorff reported that German forces had been weakened and the Soviets had started to reach the edge of the city. Only 2 hours and 40 minutes later Erdmannsdorff stated that the only part of the city still under his control was the city center and hand to hand combat was starting to take place. The last radio message that was received from Mogilev was at 11 o'clock in the evening.

After the Soviet troops defeated "Fortress Mogilev", Erdmannsdorff was captured by Soviet troops. He was tried by a Soviet tribunal (the Minsk Trial) for crimes committed in Belarus along with 18 other defendants, 14 of whom, including Erdmannsdorff, were sentenced to death on 29 January 1946. Erdmannsdorff was condemned on charges including the deportation of 10,000 people, the destruction of villages, schools and churches, and the shootings of disabled people during the construction of fortifications, the use of people as human shields, and the organization of reprisals operations against civilians under the guise of fighting partisans, and the establishment of camps in which many people died. The officers were hanged in public (with over 100,000 civilian spectators) in the horse racing venue of Minsk, on 30 January 1946. He was the younger brother of General der Infanterie Werner von Erdmannsdorff.

airline baggage rules

Airline baggage rules have become a maze of numbers, fees, and fine print that can catch even seasoned travelers off guard. Most carriers still distinguish between carry-on and checked luggage, each with its own size and weight limits that vary by airline, fare class, and route. A typical U.S. domestic carrier allows a single piece of carry-on that does not exceed 22 by 14 by 9 inches, plus a personal item like a laptop bag. For checked bags, the standard weight cap sits at 50 pounds for economy passengers, though many airlines charge extra for anything above that threshold.

International flights often bring a different set of allowances. Some European carriers permit two checked pieces for economy travelers, each weighing up to 23 kilograms, while many Asian airlines stick to a single 30-kilogram bag. The size rule, usually expressed as a linear dimension sum (length + width + height), typically caps at 158 centimeters. If a suitcase exceeds either the weight or the size limit, airlines impose surcharges that can range from $50 to $300, depending on the route and the airline's policy.

Special items such as musical instruments, sports equipment, or medical devices rarely fit neatly into the standard categories. Most airlines treat these as either oversized or overweight baggage, requiring a separate fee and sometimes advance notice at check-in. A violin, for instance, might travel as a regular carry-on if it fits inside a case under the size limit, but a larger cello usually needs to be checked and may attract an oversized charge. Passengers with mobility aids or essential medical equipment should contact the airline beforehand to arrange for complimentary handling, as many carriers waive fees for items that are deemed necessary for health or safety.

Frequent flyers should also watch out for the subtle ways loyalty status can affect baggage allowances. Platinum or Diamond members on many programs receive an extra checked bag for free and higher weight limits, sometimes up to 70 pounds per piece. Conversely, basic economy tickets often strip away the complimentary checked bag, leaving travelers to pay the standard fee even for a small suitcase. Understanding the fare rules before booking can save both money and time at the airport, especially when airlines have introduced "bag-free" promotions that only apply to specific routes or travel dates.

Finally, the rise of low-cost carriers has intensified the importance of reading the fine print. Airlines such as Spirit, Frontier, and Ryanair often advertise low base fares, but then charge for virtually every piece of luggage, even a small backpack that would normally be considered a personal item. These fees are usually collected during the online check-in process, and the cost can jump dramatically if the bag is added at the gate. To avoid unpleasant surprises, travelers should measure and weigh their bags at home, compare the airline's baggage policy with the fare they have purchased, and decide whether paying for a higher-priced ticket that includes baggage is the more economical choice.

Airline baggage rules have become a maze of numbers, fees, and fine print that can catch even seasoned travelers off guard. Most carriers still distinguish between carry-on and checked luggage, each with its own size and weight limits that vary by airline, fare class, and route. A typical U.S. domestic carrier allows a single piece of carry-on that does not exceed 22 by 14 by 9 inches, plus a personal item like a laptop bag. For checked bags, the standard weight cap sits at 50 pounds for economy passengers, though many airlines charge extra for anything above that threshold.

International flights often bring a different set of allowances. Some European carriers permit two checked pieces for economy travelers, each weighing up to 23 kilograms, while many Asian airlines stick to a single 30-kilogram bag. The size rule, usually expressed as a linear dimension sum (length + width + height), typically caps at 158 centimeters. If a suitcase exceeds either the weight or the size limit, airlines impose surcharges that can range from $50 to $300, depending on the route and the airline's policy.

Special items such as musical instruments, sports equipment, or medical devices rarely fit neatly into the standard categories. Most airlines treat these as either oversized or overweight baggage, requiring a separate fee and sometimes advance notice at check-in. A violin, for instance, might travel as a regular carry-on if it fits inside a case under the size limit, but a larger cello usually needs to be checked and may attract an oversized charge. Passengers with mobility aids or essential medical equipment should contact the airline beforehand to arrange for complimentary handling, as many carriers waive fees for items that are deemed necessary for health or safety.

The purpose of this memorandum is to provide staff, volunteers, and partners with a concise overview of mountain weather conditions that can be expected during the upcoming field season. Understanding how temperature, wind, precipitation, and solar radiation behave at altitude is essential for planning safe operations, protecting equipment, and ensuring that visitors receive accurate briefings before embarking on trail excursions.

In the lower foothills, weather often follows the patterns observed in the surrounding valleys, with daytime highs ranging from the mid-50s to low 70s Fahrenheit in spring and early summer. As elevation increases, temperatures drop roughly three degrees per 1,000 feet, so at 9,000 feet the same day may feel like the mid-30s. Diurnal temperature swings are pronounced; clear nights can plunge below freezing even after a warm afternoon. Cloud cover tends to develop in the late afternoon as moist air is forced upward, forming orographic clouds that can quickly thicken into low-level fog or stratus.

Wind speed and direction are highly variable and can change without warning. Valley breezes often shift to downslope katabatic winds after sunset, while ridge tops may experience gusts exceeding 40 mph during storm passages. Sudden squalls are common in the spring, especially when frontal systems intersect with the mountain barrier. These gusts can create dangerous wind chill values and increase the risk of falling debris, such as loose rocks or ice. Precipitation is typically localized; a storm that bypasses a valley may dump several inches of snow on a summit while leaving lower elevations dry.

Forecasting tools must be used in conjunction with on-site observation. The National Weather Service provides high-resolution mountain models that are updated every six hours, but they often underestimate convective activity. Portable weather stations, wind anemometers, and temperature loggers should be deployed at key elevations to capture real-time data. Staff should check both regional forecasts and site-specific readings at the start of each shift, and any significant deviation from expected conditions should trigger an immediate reassessment of planned activities.

All personnel should be equipped with layered clothing, waterproof outer shells, and head protection. Emergency kits must include a lightweight bivouac shelter, high-energy rations, and a reliable means of communication. When the forecast calls for rapid temperature drops or high winds, groups should limit exposure to exposed ridgelines and avoid night travel unless absolutely necessary. Routine briefings should reinforce the "turn back early" principle, especially when clouds obscure the trail or visibility falls below 50 feet.

By maintaining vigilance, employing accurate forecasting, and adhering to the safety protocols outlined above, we can minimize weather-related incidents and ensure a productive and enjoyable season for everyone involved.

raw:
clinic appointment reminder

Missed medical appointments remain a persistent challenge for healthcare providers and patients alike, costing the system billions of dollars annually in wasted resources and disrupted schedules. When a patient fails to show up for a scheduled consultation, the immediate consequence is an underutilized slot that cannot easily be refilled with last-minute bookings. This inefficiency creates a ripple effect, delaying care for other patients who might have benefited from that specific time frame. Understanding the mechanics behind automated appointment reminders is therefore essential for anyone navigating the modern healthcare landscape, whether as a provider looking to optimize efficiency or a patient seeking to maintain consistent care.

The primary mechanism of these systems relies on multi-channel communication strategies to ensure the message reaches the intended recipient. Most platforms now default to sending initial notifications via secure email, followed by a text message reminder approximately twenty-four hours before the appointment. For patients who have opted into additional touches, a final voice call may be placed the morning of the visit. This layered approach significantly increases the likelihood that the patient is aware of the commitment. The systems are designed to track engagement, allowing the clinic to know instantly if a patient confirms receipt or declines the appointment, thus freeing up the calendar for others immediately.

From the patient's perspective, these reminders serve as a critical cognitive aid in an increasingly complex daily routine. Modern life is filled with competing priorities, from work deadlines to family obligations, making it easy for a non-urgent GP visit or a routine specialist check-up to be overlooked. A well-timed digital nudge anchors the appointment in the patient's immediate schedule, reducing the mental load required to remember specific dates. Furthermore, many reminder services include helpful contextual information, such as parking instructions, fasting requirements, or what to bring, which reduces anxiety and the likelihood of no-shows due to confusion or uncertainty about the visit.

However, the implementation of these systems is not without its nuances and potential pitfalls. Excessive notifications can lead to alert fatigue, where patients begin to ignore messages from the healthcare provider. Clinics must balance the need for visibility with the risk of becoming a nuisance. Moreover, technical glitches can occur, where messages bounce back or arrive out of order, causing unnecessary distress. Patients who switch mobile numbers without updating their medical records often find themselves missing critical updates, highlighting the importance of keeping personal contact information current in all healthcare portals and physical files.

The long-term benefits of effective appointment reminder systems extend beyond simple attendance rates. They contribute to more accurate demographic data, streamlined revenue cycles, and overall higher quality of care by ensuring continuity. When patients consistently attend scheduled visits, medical histories are updated regularly, and chronic conditions are managed proactively rather than reactively. For clinics, the reduction in no-shows translates directly to financial stability and improved staff morale, as providers are not left waiting or forced to double up on cancellations. Ultimately, a robust reminder system acts as a bridge between the clinical team and the patient, fostering a relationship built on mutual respect for time and health.

raw:
office relocation

Moving an office to a new location can feel like a daunting project, but with a clear plan and the right partners, it becomes an opportunity to boost productivity and morale. The first step is to map out a realistic timeline that aligns with business cycles, avoiding peak sales periods or major client deadlines. By setting milestones for packing, transport, and setup, you keep everyone informed and reduce the risk of costly delays.

A thorough inventory is essential before any boxes are sealed. Sort through furniture, equipment, and supplies, deciding what to keep, sell, or donate. This not only lightens the load but also cuts moving expenses and frees up space in the new office. Label each item with its destination room and, if possible, a brief description to simplify unpacking and avoid misplacements.

Choosing a reputable moving company with experience in office relocations makes a big difference. Look for firms that offer insurance, climate-controlled transport for sensitive electronics, and a track record of meeting tight deadlines. A detailed contract that outlines responsibilities, insurance coverage, and contingency plans for unexpected obstacles, such as elevator outages or parking restrictions, protects both parties and provides peace of mind.

Technology transition deserves special attention. Schedule IT specialists to back up data, disconnect servers, and re-wire networks at the new site before employees arrive. Test the internet connection, phone lines, and any cloud-based services to ensure a seamless switch-over. A brief downtime is inevitable, but careful coordination can keep it to a few hours, minimizing disruption to client communication and internal workflows.

Finally, communicate openly with staff throughout the move. Share updates on the schedule, provide packing guidelines, and invite feedback on the new layout. A welcome kit with a floor plan, key contacts, and local amenities helps employees settle in quickly. When the move is complete, celebrate the fresh start with a small office gathering; it reinforces team spirit and marks the beginning of a new chapter in a space designed for growth.

Trisiras

Trishiras (Sanskrit: त्रिशिरस्, romanized: Triśiras, lit. 'One with three heads'), also referred to as Vishvarupa, was the three-headed son of the craftsman god Tvashta. He was killed by Indra, the king of the devas. To avenge his death, Tvashta later created the demon Vritra.

In the Rigveda, Vishvarupa is the son of the god Tvashta/Tvashtr and the guardian of cows. He is an enemy of Indra, the king of the gods, who comes into conflict with him. Indra is victorious in the conflict and Aptya (an ally of Indra) kills Vishvarupa, and Vishvarupa is then beheaded by Indra. Another verse states that Indra stole Vishvarupa's cattle and released them. The Brihaddevata narrates that Vishvarupa is the son of Tvashta and his asura wife, and the twin of Saranyu. He is sent by the demons to become the priest of the devas, desiring to destroy them. Indra suspected his intentions and beheaded him. His three heads turn into three different birds. Furious by the demise of his son, Tvashtr creates a demon called Vritra to avenge his death.

Viçvarupa, son of Tvastr, was the domestic priest of the gods, and the sister's son of the Asuras. He had three heads, one which drank Soma, one alcohol, and one which ate food. He promised openly the share to the Gods, secretly to the Asuras. Men promise openly the share to every one; if they promise any one secretly, his share is indeed promised. Therefore Indra was afraid (thinking), 'Such an one is diverting the sovereignty (from me).' He took his bolt and smote off his heads. (The head) which drank Soma became a hazelcock; (the head) which drank alcohol a sparrow; (the head) which ate food a partridge.

According to the Udyoga Parva of the epic Mahabharata and the Devi Bhagavata Purana, Tvashta had a conflict with Indra and wanted to dethrone him. With his wife Virocana (or Rechana), who was the daughter of Prahlada and belonged to Asura race, Tvashta had Trishiras, who was born with three heads. His three heads were each named Somapītha, Surāpītha, and Annāda as each head consumed Soma, Sura, and food, respectively. It is also told that one head was responsible for drinking; with another head, he observed his surroundings; and with his last head, he read the Vedas. Trishiras grew powerful and performed penance to become more powerful. Indra became frightened of him, and sent Apsaras (nymphs) to seduce him and break his penance. However, Trisharas was unaffected and Indra went to him and killed him using his thunderbolt. He was concerned about the possibility of Trishiras reviving, so he sent a carpenter to cut off each of his heads. From the head that chanted Vedic mantras rose the Kapiñjala birds; from the head used for drinking soma rose the Kalapiṅga birds and from the third head rose the Tittiri birds. Tvashta performed a yajna, from which Vritra emerged to avenge Trishiras's death. The Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata, Bhagavata Purana, Brahmavaivarta Purana narrates a different myth about Vishvarupa and portray him as a guru or priest of Indra. According to this version, Brihaspati, the guru of the devas (gods), refused to perform yajna (ritual) after he was insulted by Indra. This led the devas to lose to their enemies, the Asuras. On the advice of the creator god Brahma, Indra appointed Vishvarupa, the son of Tvashta and Rechana, as the new priest of the sacrifice. However, Vishvarupa was also related to the Asuras through his mother and didn't perform the sacrifice appropriately. Indra suspected his allegiance and beheaded Vishvarupa. These texts state that Indra sinned Brahmanahatya (murder of a Brahman) for killing Trishiras, who was both a Brahmana and his guru. The Brahmavaivarta Purana also attests that Vishvarupa had a son named Sutapa.

Boroughmuir Blaze Basketball Club

The club was founded in 1961 with an initial nucleus of players from Edinburgh's Boroughmuir High School. The club's heyday came in the late 1960s when players like Tony Wilson, Mel Capaldi, John Tunnah, Brian Carmichael and Bill McInnes went on to form the backbone of the Scotland national basketball team. A highlight of this period came in 1967 when Boroughmuir became the first British team to participate in a European cup competition. They were drawn against the mighty Real Madrid and played their home tie at Murrayfield Ice Rink before a crowd of nearly 1,000.

The Blaze moniker was introduced in 2004 and in recent years the club has rejuvenated its development program with the club now having over 100 members with teams at every age group from Under 12 through to Over 50s. The club's growth is reflected by entry in the U16 National League since 2005/06 and the U18 National League from 2006/07. The Senior Men's team re-entered the National League in 2011 after 3 years away, and won their first National League title in 38 years, and completed the league-playoffs double, in 2016. In season 2022/23 Blaze senior men won the domestic treble - league, cup and post season play-offs.

Bill McInnes enjoyed a distinguished playing career with Boroughmuir in Edinburgh; he was a member of the team which dominated domestically in Scotland the 1960s and 1970s, and were British Rose Bowl champions in 1972. He also played on Boroughmuir teams that entered the FIBA European Champions Cup and FIBA European Cup Winners' Cup on five occasions in that time. He represented both Scotland and Great Britain on 176 occasions, starting all his 28 competitive GB games, and finishing as the leading scorer in eight of them. He was the leading scorer in the 1968 European Pre-Olympic event with 119 points in seven games. He was the second top scorer in 3 other Olympic qualifying events, finishing with 354 points, for a 12.6ppg average. Off the court, Bill was a founder member of Boroughmuir. Bill coached at all levels and was secretary to the club since 1961. He later served as Chair of the British Basketball Federation, was a member of the National Olympic Committee, Chair of the British Masters Basketball Association and was a director with Basketball Scotland, which he previously chaired from 1990 to 2008. He was awarded the FIBA Order of Merit posthumously after his death in 2017.

Prior to the 1997-98 season, Boroughmuir competed in every National League season since its formation in 1969, winning 9 of their 10 league titles to date consecutively (1969-70, 1970-71, 1971-72, 1972-73, 1973-74, 1974-75, 1975-76, 1976-77, 1977-78).

raw:
water quality report

The annual water quality report released by the municipal utility last week gives a clear snapshot of the drinking water from our taps. It lists the sources, treatment steps, and results of laboratory tests performed over the past year. Residents can now see how the water measures up against state and federal standards.

The report includes levels of chlorine, lead, copper, and microbial contaminants such as E. coli. Each contaminant is shown with its concentration, the applicable maximum contaminant level (MCL), and a simple pass-or-fail sign. Trend data compare this year's results with the previous three years to highlight any change.

Reading the numbers is straightforward. A lead concentration below 0.015 mg/L meets EPA safety limits, and a chlorine residual between 0.2 and 2.0 mg/L indicates effective disinfection. When a value exceeds its MCL, the utility must issue a consumer advisory and outline corrective actions.

In our city, the latest figures show a modest rise in copper, though still well under the 1.3 mg/L limit. The utility attributes the increase to aging pipework in older neighborhoods and plans to replace affected lines over the next two years.

The full PDF is available on the utility's website, and printed copies can be requested by phone. Monitoring the water quality report helps residents ask questions, demand transparency, and protect their health.

raw:
community garden

The old vacant lot on Maple Street has been transformed into a vibrant community garden, a testament to what happens when neighbors decide to collaborate rather than compete. Six months ago, it was an overgrown patch of crabgrass and scattered debris, largely ignored by the city and the passersby who hurried past on their way to the bus stop. Today, the air smells of rich soil, blooming zinnias, and the faint, earthy scent of wet compost. The transformation began with a single flyer posted on the community board and a group of twelve residents who shared a similar frustration: a wasted space in a neighborhood that desperately needed green. They booked a Saturday session, brought shovels, and started digging.

Getting the permits was the first major hurdle, but the physical labor proved to be where the true community spirit emerged. Volunteers arrived in waves, some with prior gardening experience and others who had never held a trowel in their lives. The learning curve was steep for many, but the atmosphere remained light and encouraging. Elders in the community offered advice on how to amend the sandy soil, while younger residents handled the heavy lifting of moving timber and building raised beds. The division of labor was organic, dictated by who showed up and what skills they naturally possessed, creating a dynamic that felt far more authentic than any organized project could achieve.

Now that the infrastructure is in place, the garden operates on a simple yet effective system of shared responsibility. Each family or small group has been assigned four-foot plots, but the path remains open to anyone who wants to swing by. There are no strict guards or time limits; if a plot looks neglected, a neighbor might step in to pull weeds or check the irrigation timers. This informal oversight has led to a stronger sense of accountability among the participants. People take pride not just in their own crops but in the overall health of the space, ensuring that the common areas, such as the tool shed and the water tap, are kept clean and functional for the next person who arrives.

The harvest has been the highlight of the past two seasons, but the social yield has been even more significant. On Friday evenings, as the sun begins to dip below the rowan trees, the garden becomes a meeting place. Families gather to share the fresh vegetables they have picked, turning a simple salad into a conversation starter. Strangers who once only nodded from their cars now know each other by name, discussing everything from municipal zoning laws to favorite recipes using local produce. The barriers of social isolation that often define urban living seem to dissolve when people are side by side, hands in the dirt, working toward a common tangible goal.

As the season winds down and plans for next year's planting begin, the lessons from this experiment are clear. A community garden is not merely about producing food; it is about cultivating connection. It proves that with a little bit of grit, a shared vision, and the willingness to show up, even the most overlooked parts of a city can become hubs of life and learning. The garden has shown that while we cannot always control the weather or the economy, we can certainly control how we treat the ground beneath our feet and each other. This patch of land on Maple Street is no longer just scenery; it is the heart of the neighborhood, thriving in the collective effort of its members.

raw:
Paul Rester

Paul Rester is the director of the Joint Intelligence Group at the United States' Guantanamo Bay detention camps, in Cuba-the Chief Interrogator. Rester described the interrogation techniques the military used at Guantanamo to the Associated Press. He said he was concerned that the CIA's use of "extended interrogation techniques" had given the public the wrong impression of the techniques the military used at Guantanamo.

Everybody in the world believes that they know how we do what we do, and I have to endure it every time I turn around and somebody is making reference to waterboarding. Rester told Andrew Selsky of the Associated Press that the successes of the American military interrogators had come through "rapport-building" techniques-not coercive or brutal techniques. He said Joint Task Force Guantanamo commander Mark Buzby had authorized him to describe one of the interrogators recent successes.

For security reasons, he would only discuss one of the successes, and that was only because his boss, Rear Adm. Mark Buzby, already had described it in a speech last month. Buzby said several detainees, using poster board paper and crayons, drew detailed maps of the Tora Bora area in eastern Afghanistan that enabled coalition forces to wipe out safe houses, trenches and supplies last summer as Taliban forces were returning to the stronghold they had abandoned more than five years ago. Rester acknowledged that Mohammed al Qahtani, and one other captive, had been subjected to rougher treatment in 2002. He didn't offer the name of the other captive who had been subjected to rougher treatment. Time Magazine reported that Mohammed al Qahtani's interrogation log had been leaked to them, and that it documented he had been subjected to almost two months of sleep deprivation, forced nudity, force-feedings, forced enemas, threats against his family, and sexual humiliation. According to Selsky's article Joshua Colangelo-Bryan, a lawyer who volunteered to help Guantanamo captives "scoffed at Rester's contention that rough treatment at Guantanamo was restricted to just two men."

There are so many accounts by FBI agents ... and others who personally saw non-rapport-building techniques that Rester's statement is just not credible. Following the United States Supreme Court's ruling in Hamdan v. Rumsfeld Rester stated:

raw:
hiking trail conditions

Before lacing up your boots and heading to the trailhead, taking a few minutes to check current hiking trail conditions can make all the difference for a safe and enjoyable outing. Trails are dynamic environments, constantly changing due to weather, wildlife, and human activity. A quick check can prevent unexpected hazards and ensure you're adequately prepared for what lies ahead.

Current conditions might include muddy sections from recent rainfall, especially in low-lying areas or north-facing slopes where moisture lingers. Higher elevations or shaded canyons might still hold lingering patches of snow or ice, even well into spring. Watch out for downed trees blocking paths, which can create difficult detours, and be aware of potentially swollen stream crossings after significant precipitation.

Reliable information often comes from official sources. Check the specific park or forest service website for the trail you plan to hike; these sites are regularly updated by rangers. User-submitted reports on apps like AllTrails or dedicated local hiking forums can also offer valuable, real-time insights, but always cross-reference if possible. Don't hesitate to call a local ranger station directly for the most precise details.

Remember that weather forecasts aren't just for your comfort; they directly impact trail safety. Heavy rains can lead to flash floods in narrow canyons or make steep, rocky sections treacherous. Extreme heat increases the risk of dehydration and heatstroke, while sudden drops in temperature can bring unexpected snow or icy conditions, particularly at higher altitudes.

Armed with accurate condition reports, you can adjust your plans accordingly. Perhaps you'll opt for waterproof boots instead of trail runners, pack microspikes for icy patches, or even choose an alternative, less challenging route. If conditions seem too difficult or unsafe, it's always wise to postpone your trip or select a different trail. Your safety is paramount, and a prepared hiker is a happy hiker.

raw:
university admissions

The application season is underway, and for thousands of students, the process begins with a mountain of paperwork, essays, and strategic planning. University admissions is no longer just about maintaining high grades. It is a holistic evaluation that looks at character, leadership, and unique personal experiences. Understanding this shift is the first step toward a successful application. Many prospective students still believe that a perfect GPA guarantees acceptance, but that is rarely the case anymore. Admissions officers are seeking diversity of thought and background, which means your extracurricular activities and personal narrative carry significant weight.

Start by defining what you are looking for in a college environment. Do you want a large research institution with vast resources, or a smaller liberal arts college with close-knit faculty? Researching these differences helps you create a balanced list of safety, match, and reach schools. It is crucial to visit campuses whenever possible. Walking the halls and sitting in on a class can tell you more about the culture than any brochure ever could. This personal connection often comes through in your essays, making your application stand out from the thousands of others on an admissions officer's desk.

The personal essay is the heart of your application. This is your chance to tell your story in your own voice. Avoid generic topics like winning a game or a standard summer job. Instead, focus on a specific moment of growth, a challenge you overcame, or a unique perspective you bring to the table. Authenticity resonates. Admissions officers read thousands of these essays and can quickly spot a formulaic approach. Let your personality shine through, and be honest about your failures and lessons learned. This vulnerability creates a human connection that numbers alone cannot achieve.

Financial aid and scholarship applications often go hand-in-hand with the admission process. Many students overlook the fact that being admitted does not mean you can afford to attend. Start preparing your FAFSA and relevant institutional forms early. Some schools have specific deadlines that differ from the general application dates. Understanding the financial landscape helps you make educated decisions. It also allows you to negotiate offers if multiple schools show strong interest in recruiting you.

Finally, remember that rejection is not a defeat. It is simply a mismatch at that particular moment. If your first choice does not work out, there are always other excellent options waiting for you. Stay organized, check your emails regularly, and keep a positive mindset. The journey will be stressful, but the outcome will shape the next four years of your life in profound ways. Focus on finding the community that aligns with your goals, and the right path will reveal itself.

raw:
climate adaptation

Climate adaptation has moved from a niche concern to a central pillar of municipal planning, as extreme weather events become more frequent and severe. Cities are now integrating flood-resilient infrastructure, heat-mitigating green spaces, and water-conserving policies into everyday operations. The shift reflects a growing recognition that mitigation alone cannot shield communities from the inevitable impacts of a warming planet.

In practice, adaptation begins with detailed risk assessments that map vulnerable neighborhoods, critical utilities, and ecological hotspots. Planners overlay climate projections-rising sea levels, temperature spikes, and altered precipitation patterns-onto existing data to pinpoint where interventions are most needed. This evidence-based approach helps prioritize projects that deliver the greatest protective benefit while staying within budget constraints.

One of the most visible adaptations is the redesign of public spaces to cope with heat stress. Urban trees, reflective pavements, and shaded corridors not only lower ambient temperatures but also improve air quality and public health. When combined with community-driven cooling centers, these measures provide immediate relief during heatwaves, especially for seniors and low-income residents who lack access to climate-controlled environments.

Water management strategies have also evolved dramatically. Instead of relying solely on large dams, many municipalities are investing in decentralized solutions like rain gardens, permeable sidewalks, and restored wetlands. These features capture stormwater at its source, reducing flood risk while recharging groundwater supplies. By treating water as a renewable resource rather than a static commodity, cities build resilience against both droughts and intense storms.

The success of climate adaptation hinges on inclusive governance. Engaging local residents, businesses, and indigenous groups ensures that solutions respect cultural values and address real-world needs. Transparent decision-making, paired with continuous monitoring, allows policies to be refined as climate science advances. In this collaborative framework, adaptation becomes not just a technical challenge but a shared societal commitment to safeguard the future.

raw:
volunteer onboarding

Volunteer onboarding is often treated as a secondary task after staffing the paid roles are filled. This oversight creates friction in the very first week. New recruits arrive with high energy but zero structural support. Without a clear roadmap, enthusiasm quickly dissipates into confusion. Organizations lose valuable hours correcting misunderstandings that a proper introduction would have prevented. The initial days set the tone for long-term engagement.

Start by sending a personalized welcome email before the first day. Include the start time, location, and what to wear. Attach a brief orientation packet covering mission statements and safety protocols. This proactive step reduces first-day anxiety. It signals that the organization values the volunteer's time and contribution. The document serves as a reliable reference point when questions arise later during the first shift.

Assign a dedicated onboarding buddy on the first day. This peer mentor answers questions that a manager might not have time to address. The buddy walks the volunteer through the environment and introduces key staff members. Human connection accelerates cultural integration significantly. The volunteer feels less like an outsider and more like a team member. This social linkage is often the strongest predictor of volunteer retention.

Provide structured training tailored to the specific role. General overviews are insufficient for tasks requiring safety compliance or technical skills. Break down complex duties into manageable steps. Offer resources like quick start guides or video tutorials. Check for understanding regularly rather than assuming comprehension. Active feedback loops ensure the volunteer feels confident in their abilities before handling independent tasks.

Follow up within the first month with a structured check-in. Ask specific questions about clarity, resources, and satisfaction. Identify friction points before they become reasons for quitting. Celebrate small wins to reinforce behavior. A robust onboarding process transforms temporary help into lasting commitment. It builds a pipeline of reliable, knowledgeable individuals who understand the organization's unique ecosystem deeply.

January 5 - A Libyan warplane bombs a Greek-operated oil tanker anchored offshore the city of Derna, killing two sailors, one Greek and one Romanian. The Greek government condemned what it called an "unprovoked and cowardly" attack and demanded an investigation and punishment for those responsible. January 18 - State-sponsored army and Islamist-sponsored opposition declare a ceasefire. January 27 - Five gunmen at the Libyan Corinthia Hotel in Tripoli attack with at least ten dead. The hotel was previously the location in 2013 where a former prime minister was abducted.

February 4 - Gunmen storm the al-Mabrook oil field. February 15 - The Islamic State releases a video purportedly showing the beheading of 21 Egyptian Coptic Christians who had been previously kidnapped in Sirte. February 16 - Egypt bombs Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant targets in the city of Derna in Libya following the execution of 21 Coptic Christians. February 20 - Multiple car bombs kill at least 45 and wound 30 in al-Qubbah.

March 2 - The House of Representatives agrees to resume UN brokered peace talks with a rival government. March 15 - Fighting rages near Sirte between Islamic State and a militia alliance. March 16 - Islamic State kidnaps about 20 medical workers from the Ibn Sina Hospital in Sirte.

April 13 - Nine people are killed and 400+ reported missing when a migrant vessel sinks off the Libyan coast. April 16 - Four immigrants arriving in Sicily claim to be the only survivors of a sunken ship. They say that 41 people had drowned when their vessel overturned and sank shortly after departing from Libya.

raw:
moving checklist

The first step in any successful relocation is creating a comprehensive moving checklist. This document serves as your master plan, ensuring that no critical task is overlooked in the rush of packing and transportation. Start by dividing your checklist into three main categories: tasks to handle thirty days before the move, actions for the week prior, and final steps for moving day. This structured approach helps you manage your time effectively and reduces the overall stress of the transition.

Administrative tasks often cause the most confusion if left until the last minute. Spend the first week of your preparation updating your address with all relevant parties. This includes your bank, credit card companies, insurance providers, and any ongoing subscriptions you may have. Additionally, obtain storage unit reservations if you plan to keep bulk items for later, and download copies of important documents to secure digital backups.

Packing should begin gradually rather than in a frantic sprint during the final day. Start with non-essential items from infrequently used rooms like the guest bedroom or the basement. Label each box clearly with its contents and the room it belongs to. This simple practice saves hours on moving day when the movers are unloading, allowing you to set up your new space with precision and speed without searching through chaotic piles of cardboard.

As moving day approaches, focus on gathering your essentials into a separate, easily accessible bag. This bag should contain vital documents, basic toiletries, charger cables, a change of clothes, and any prescriptions or baby supplies. Renting the moving truck or hiring professionals requires final confirmation a few days out. Ensure you have the necessary permits if you are moving manually, and plan your route in advance to avoid unexpected traffic delays on the big day.

Finally, do not forget to secure your new home before arriving. If you are renting, confirm the check-in process with your landlord. If you are buying, verify that utilities have been transferred to your name. Having water, electricity, and internet ready upon arrival makes the transition significantly smoother. A well-executed checklist turns a daunting logistical challenge into a manageable series of small, actionable steps, allowing you to focus on settling into your new life rather than wrestling with forgotten details.

raw:
sourdough baking

Sourdough has surged from a niche hobby to a kitchen staple, drawing bakers with its tangy flavor and rustic charm. The magic begins with a starter, a living culture of wild yeasts and lactobacilli that feeds on flour and water. Keeping it happy requires daily feedings, a warm spot, and a bit of patience as the microbes mature.

When the starter is bubbly and aromatic, the dough can be mixed. A simple formula-flour, water, starter, and a pinch of salt-lets the natural leaven do the heavy lifting. After a gentle autolyse, the dough rests, then undergoes a series of folds that develop gluten without intensive kneading. This slow, hands-on approach creates the open crumb that sourdough lovers adore.

Proofing is where time becomes an ally. A bulk rise at room temperature for several hours, followed by a cold retard in the refrigerator, deepens flavor and improves the crust. Shaping the loaf into a tight boule or a long batard seals the surface, ready for the final rise. A well-heated oven, often with a steam source like a preheated Dutch oven, yields that coveted caramelized crust.

Scoring the loaf isn't just decorative; it directs the expansion of gases and prevents uneven tearing. A confident slash, followed by a burst of steam, produces a crackling sound as the bread erupts in the heat. The result is a loaf with a crisp edge and a tender, airy interior.

Freshly baked sourdough pairs beautifully with everything from buttered olive oil to sharp cheese. Slice it while still warm, toast the leftovers, or freeze portions for later. With each bake, the starter evolves, and the baker hones a rhythm that turns a simple mixture of flour and water into a living, breathing loaf.

Subject: Welcome to the Community Shelter Volunteer Team
Hello Alex,
Thank you for donating your time and energy to our community shelter. We are thrilled to welcome you to the team. Your enthusiasm during the interview was contagious, and we are confident that your skills will make a significant difference in the lives of the residents we serve every day.
Before you start your first shift, we need to complete a few administrative tasks. Please review the attached volunteer handbook, which covers our code of conduct, safety protocols, and operational expectations. We require all new volunteers to sign the liability waiver and complete the basic safety training module. This process usually takes less than twenty minutes and ensures everyone feels secure in the work environment.
To help you acclimate, we will pair you with a seasoned volunteer mentor for your initial three shifts. They will introduce you to the daily routines, key staff members, and specific needs of the residents. This supportive approach allows you to ask questions and learn from experience without feeling overwhelmed by the immediate demands of the role.
Regarding scheduling, we have assigned you to the Tuesday evening welcome shift for the next four weeks. This allows us to observe your workflow and provides you with a predictable routine. Please let us know if any conflicts arise with this schedule so we can adjust your assignments accordingly. Flexibility is key here, as volunteer coverage can sometimes be thin.
If you have any immediate questions, please do not hesitate to reach out. We are a close-knit group, and no question is too small. We look forward to seeing you on your first day and starting this meaningful journey together. Your compassion is exactly what our community needs right now.
Sincerely,
Sarah Jenkins
Program Coordinator

raw:
baby sleep routines

.

Most parents have discovered that a consistent bedtime act can be the difference between a peaceful night and hours of whining. Building a reliable sleep ritual signals to your infant's developing brain that it is time to wind down. Start by dimming the lights in your home at least thirty minutes before bedtime to encourage the production of melatonin, the natural hormone that regulates sleep cycles. This gradual transition helps prevent your baby from becoming overtired and cranky, which often makes it harder for them to settle into slumber.

The core of a successful routine often involves a short, calming sequence of activities that remain the same every night. For many families, this includes a warm bath, followed by gentle grooming and the application of soft lotion. Changing into fresh pajamas provides a tactile cue that sleep is near, while a quiet story or soft lullaby offers auditory comfort. Avoid introducing new toys or exciting books during this window, as stimulation can reverse the winding-down process you have carefully established.

Consistency is perhaps the most critical factor in making any routine work. Try to perform these steps in the same order every evening, aiming for a specific bed time window that aligns with your baby's typical sleep pressure. If your toddler is waking up at a consistent time, working backward from that wake-up time can help you determine when to start the ritual. Keep in mind that while younger infants may need different intervals, the principle of predictability remains universally effective for soothing a young mind.

It is also helpful to observe your baby's unique comfort items during this process. Some children find deep pressure from a weighted blanket or a specific stuffed animal particularly reassuring. Others may prefer to be held while you finish the last page of their book. Pay attention to what works best for your specific child, as individual preferences can vary widely. Adjusting the routine based on gentle feedback ensures that bedtime feels safe rather than like a forced demand.

Finally, be patient with the process, as establishing a solid sleep pattern can take several weeks of trial and error. There will be nights when the routine feels disrupted, and that is completely normal. When setbacks occur, return to your established steps without anger or frustration. Your calm demeanor sets the emotional tone for the evening, helping your baby feel secure enough to let go of the day and drift into restful sleep.

raw:
city council agenda

The city council agenda is the roadmap that guides each weekly meeting, outlining every item the council will discuss, vote on, or defer. It serves as a public record, ensuring transparency and giving residents a clear view of municipal priorities.

Every agenda begins with routine matters such as the approval of minutes from the previous session and public comments, followed by reports from standing committees on topics ranging from public safety to environmental stewardship. These sections are often the most predictable, but they set the tone for the more substantive decisions that follow.

Recent agendas have highlighted a surge in infrastructure projects, including the approval of a new bike lane network and the allocation of funds for street resurfacing in underserved neighborhoods. At the same time, the council is reviewing a proposed zoning amendment that could reshape a historic district, prompting strong interest from both developers and preservationists.

Citizens can access the full agenda online through the city's official website, where PDFs are posted at least 48 hours before the meeting. Many neighborhoods also receive printed copies at community centers, and local newspapers frequently publish a summary of the most pressing items.

If you want your voice heard, plan to attend the public comment segment, submit a written statement in advance, or contact your councilmember directly. Engaged residents help shape policies that affect everything from road maintenance to park programming, making the agenda a vital tool for community involvement.

Subject: Important Updates for the Upcoming Mayoral Election
Hi neighbor,
I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to share some crucial details about the local mayoral election scheduled for next month. Many residents have asked for clarification on the voting process, so I have compiled the most relevant information to help ensure your voice is heard.
First, please note that polling stations will open at seven in the morning and close at nine in the evening. The town hall lobby remains the primary location for voting, but two additional sites have been added at the elementary school and the community center to reduce wait times. These extra locations are particularly beneficial for those with mobility challenges or those who reside further from the city center.
Regarding voter identification, you will need to present a valid state-issued photo ID. Acceptable forms include a driver's license, a passport, or a military identification card. If you do not currently possess one of these documents, you can register for a free voter identification card at the election office located in the basement of town hall. They are open weekdays from nine to five for this specific purpose.
Early voting is available starting from the first day of the month through the Friday before election day. This option is highly recommended to avoid the long lines typically seen on the final day. Remember to bring your ID to the early voting sites as well, as the same verification procedures apply.
Finally, please feel free to forward this information to friends or family members who may not be following local news closely. Ensuring high voter turnout is essential for our community's future. If you have any further questions or need assistance with registration, the election office can be reached by phone during regular business hours.
Best regards,
Sarah Jenkins
