They are open weekdays from nine to five for this specific purpose.
Early voting is available starting from the first day of the month through the Friday before election day. This option is highly recommended to avoid the long lines typically seen on the final day. Remember to bring your ID to the early voting sites as well, as the same verification procedures apply.
Finally, please feel free to forward this information to friends or family members who may not be following local news closely. Ensuring high voter turnout is essential for our community's future. If you have any further questions or need assistance with registration, the election office can be reached by phone during regular business hours.
Best regards,
Sarah Jenkins

raw:
street food guide

Home | About | Contact

The allure of street food lies in its unpretentious charm and the immediacy of the experience. Unlike sit-down dining, you are immersed in the pulsing energy of the city, standing shoulder to shoulder with locals and travelers alike. The aroma of sizzling charcoal and simmering broths often serves as the first invitation, pulling you toward a bustling cart or a small family-run stall tucked into a narrow alleyway. This sensory engagement creates a connection to the local culture that no sterile restaurant can replicate. It is a raw, honest taste of daily life in the region.

Navigating a crowded food street requires a certain instinct. Look for the lines; a queue of residents waiting patiently is the most reliable indicator of quality and hygiene. Observe the cook's technique. A chef who moves with confidence and precision, keeping their station spotless despite the heat, signals a dedication to their craft. Avoid stalls that attract only tourists or those with overly elaborate English menus. Authentic vendors prioritize speed and consistency, understanding that hungry customers respect efficiency over aesthetics.

Budget preparation is essential for a successful culinary crawl. Currency exchange fees can eat into your snack budget, so keep smaller bills ready for exact change. Most street vendors operate on a cash-only basis, and carrying a bulky wallet slows down the flow. It is also wise to hydrate before you start, as many regional specialties are spicy or oily. Bringing a small, portable hand sanitizer allows you to maintain hygiene without disrupting the vibe of the evening.

Timing your visit significantly impacts the experience. Evening hours tend to offer the widest selection as vendors set up their full displays. The golden hour, just before the sun sets, provides a pleasant climate and a spectacular backdrop for photography. However, arriving slightly early means shorter waits for the most popular items. As the night deepens, the atmosphere grows more electric, with the clatter of woks and the chatter of crowds creating a symphony of urban life that invites you to lose track of time.

Ultimately, the best street food experience is one defined by curiosity rather than rigid planning. Be prepared to miss a dish while queuing for another, and embrace the spontaneity of the moment. Share plates with friends if the portions are large, and do not hesitate to ask the vendor for a small recommendation. This interactive element transforms eating from a biological necessity into a social ritual. When you finally leave the scene, your belly full and your memory bank updated, you will carry with you a unique fragment of the city's soul that no guidebook could fully capture.

The purpose of this memorandum is to outline the upcoming Spring Craft Fair scheduled for Saturday, May 18, at the Riverside Community Center. The event will run from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and will showcase local artisans, hobbyists, and small businesses offering handmade goods ranging from pottery and textiles to jewelry and woodcraft. Attendance is expected to exceed 2,000 visitors, providing an excellent opportunity for community engagement, local economic stimulation, and promotion of sustainable, handcrafted products. All participating vendors must adhere to the guidelines set forth in this document to ensure a smooth and successful fair.

All vendors are required to submit a completed application form, a copy of their business license, and proof of liability insurance no later than April 30. Applications will be reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to organizations that demonstrate a clear commitment to environmentally friendly practices, such as using recycled materials or offering biodegradable packaging. Once approved, each vendor will receive a 10-by-10-foot booth space, a table, two chairs, and access to electrical outlets upon request. Vendors should arrive by 7:30 a.m. on the day of the fair to set up their displays and must complete all setup activities by 8:45 a.m. before doors open to the public.

Health and safety protocols will be strictly enforced throughout the event. All food-related vendors must comply with the city's food handling regulations and display the required permits prominently at their booths. Hand sanitizing stations will be positioned at each entrance and throughout the venue, and vendors are encouraged to provide hand sanitizer for patrons. In the event of severe weather, the fair will be moved to the community center's indoor hall, and all vendors will be notified via text message and email at least two hours prior to the start time. Vendors should prepare for the possibility of indoor relocation by having flexible display arrangements.

Marketing efforts for the craft fair will be coordinated by the Community Outreach Department. Promotional materials, including flyers, social media posts, and local newspaper advertisements, will highlight featured vendors and special programming such as live demonstrations, a children's craft corner, and a raffle for a handcrafted gift basket. Vendors are invited to submit high-resolution images of their products and a brief description for inclusion in the promotional campaign by May 5. Additional exposure will be offered through a post-event photo gallery on the community center's website, showcasing participating artisans and encouraging repeat attendance at future events.

Finally, all volunteers and staff assigned to the craft fair must complete a brief orientation session on May 16. This session will cover crowd management, emergency procedures, and customer service expectations. Volunteers will be responsible for assisting with vendor check-in, monitoring booth compliance, and providing information to attendees. A detailed schedule and contact list will be distributed after the orientation. Should any questions arise regarding the fair's logistics, please direct them to the event coordinator, Ms. Elena Ramirez, at eramirez@rivercenter.org or by calling the office at 555-842-3100.

online privacy settings

In today's hyper-connected world, the term "online privacy" is more than a buzzword-it's a daily reality that shapes how we interact with social media, banking apps, and even the news sites we read. Every click, swipe, or tap generates data that can be stored, analyzed, and shared, often without a clear warning. Understanding the basic settings that control who sees your information is the first step toward protecting yourself from unwanted exposure, identity theft, and targeted advertising that can feel invasive. While the technology behind these platforms evolves quickly, the principles for safeguarding your personal data remain surprisingly simple.

Most major services now place privacy controls behind a series of menus that can be easy to overlook. When you sign up for a new account, take a moment to explore the "privacy" or "security" sections before you start posting. These panels usually allow you to decide whether your profile is public, visible only to friends, or hidden entirely. Adjusting these options can limit the amount of personal information displayed to strangers and reduce the chances that automated bots scrape your details for malicious purposes. Remember, the default setting is often the most permissive, so actively changing it can make a big difference.

Beyond who can see your profile, pay close attention to permissions granted to third-party apps and websites. Many platforms ask for access to your contacts, location, camera, or microphone as part of the sign-up process. While some requests are legitimate, others are unnecessary and can become a backdoor for data collection. Regularly reviewing and revoking permissions you no longer need prevents apps from silently gathering information about your habits and whereabouts. It's also wise to enable two-factor authentication wherever possible; a second verification step, such as a code sent to your phone, adds a strong layer of protection against unauthorized access.

Another often-ignored area is the handling of cookies and tracking scripts. When you browse the web, small files called cookies store details about your sessions, preferences, and browsing history. Many sites now offer a "Do Not Track" or "Cookie Settings" option that lets you limit the extent of this monitoring. Switching to a stricter setting may cause some features to break, but it also reduces the amount of data companies can compile about your online behavior. Using privacy-focused browsers or extensions can further block unwanted trackers and give you more control over what is recorded.

Finally, keep your software up to date and stay informed about new privacy policies. Vendors frequently release updates that patch security holes and sometimes introduce new privacy features. Ignoring these updates can leave you vulnerable to exploits that bypass even the most carefully configured settings. Subscribing to reputable tech news sources or following the security blog of the service you use can alert you to changes that might affect how your data is handled. By staying proactive and periodically revisiting your privacy settings, you turn the tide in favor of your own digital security.

The Finance Department issues this memorandum to outline procedures and expectations for the upcoming fiscal year budget planning cycle. All department heads must align proposals with the organization's strategic objectives and the approved spending limits for 2027. Accuracy and timeliness are essential to support operational effectiveness.

The planning window opens 1 November and closes 15 December. Each unit submits a preliminary draft to the budgeting team, receives feedback, and revises accordingly. Final approval is granted by 31 January for board review. This schedule ensures alignment with corporate goals. Early submissions will be given priority review.

Data collection is the responsibility of operational managers, who must provide recent expense reports, staffing forecasts, and capital project estimates. Finance analysts will consolidate inputs, perform variance analysis, and flag anomalies. All assumptions must be documented and verify compliance with policy.

Key considerations include alignment with the five-year strategic plan, regulatory compliance, and inflation impact on cost projections. Prioritize projects with measurable outcomes and consider phased implementation. Include risk mitigation to address potential overruns and evaluate long-term sustainability.

Submit all files to the central budgeting portal by the deadline. Direct questions to the finance help desk, extension 2245, or email the CFO. Your cooperation ensures a transparent and effective budgeting process for the coming year and adhere to the established timeline for all departments.

raw:
solar panel installation

Solar power has moved from a niche hobby to a mainstream energy solution, and homeowners are increasingly asking how they can tap into the sun's abundant electricity. The promise of lower utility bills, reduced carbon footprints, and potential tax incentives makes the idea of a solar panel system hard to ignore. Yet many people feel overwhelmed by the technical details, permitting requirements, and cost considerations that accompany a residential installation. This guide walks you through the essential steps so you can decide whether solar fits your home and budget.

The first step in any solar project is a thorough evaluation of the roof's suitability. A south-facing roof with minimal shading is ideal, but east- and west-oriented surfaces can also generate respectable output if they receive enough direct sunlight. Professionals will measure the roof's pitch, structural integrity, and available square footage to determine how many panels can be mounted safely. In addition, they will assess the orientation of nearby trees, chimneys, and neighboring buildings that might cast shadows during peak sun hours. If your roof is old or has a steep slope, reinforcing the structure or opting for a ground-mounted array may be necessary.

Local regulations and utility policies play a critical role in shaping the installation timeline. Most municipalities require a building permit and an electrical permit before work can begin, and the paperwork often includes a site plan, system specifications, and proof of contractor licensing. Utilities may also demand an interconnection agreement to allow excess electricity to flow back onto the grid, a process that can involve a net-metering application. Working with a reputable installer who is familiar with your city's codes can streamline these steps and reduce the risk of costly delays.

When the paperwork is in order, the actual installation usually takes one to three days, depending on system size and roof complexity. Technicians first secure a mounting rack to the roof rafters, ensuring a watertight seal with flashing and sealant. The solar modules are then attached to the rack, wired together in strings, and connected to an inverter that converts the DC power into usable AC electricity. The inverter is typically mounted near the main service panel, and a dedicated circuit breaker is installed to protect the home's electrical system. Once the hardware is in place, the installer conducts a performance test, verifies compliance with local codes, and schedules a final inspection with the building department.

The upfront cost of a residential solar system can range from $15,000 to $30,000 before incentives, but federal tax credits, state rebates, and utility-offered financing can lower the effective price dramatically. Many homeowners choose a power-purchase agreement or a lease to avoid large capital outlays, paying a fixed monthly fee while enjoying the energy savings. It's important to compare the total life-cycle cost of each option, factoring in the expected 25-year lifespan of most panels and the projected increase in electricity rates.

After the system is commissioned, maintenance is minimal. Panels have no moving parts, and most manufacturers offer a 25-year performance warranty that guarantees a certain output level. Periodic cleaning to remove dust or bird droppings, especially in dry climates, can keep efficiency high. An annual visual inspection by a qualified technician will catch any loose connections or degraded components early, ensuring the system continues to deliver reliable power for decades.

Local regulations and utility policies play a critical role in shaping the installation timeline. Most municipalities require a building permit and an electrical permit before work can begin, and the paperwork often includes a site plan, system specifications, and proof of contractor licensing. Utilities may also demand an interconnection agreement to allow excess electricity to flow back onto the grid, a process that can involve a net-metering application. Working with a reputable installer who is familiar with your city's codes can streamline these steps and reduce the risk of costly delays.

After the system is commissioned, maintenance is minimal. Panels have no moving parts, and most manufacturers offer a 25-year performance warranty that guarantees a certain output level. Periodic cleaning to remove dust or bird droppings, especially in dry climates, can keep efficiency high. Subject: Feedback on the new station lifts and platform gaps
Dear Service Team,
I am writing to share my recent experience using the metro system with my mobility scooter. I truly appreciate the recent updates to the boarding protocols. The staff were exceptionally patient and helpful during my last commute. However, there is still significant room for improvement in how we handle physical barriers.
The automatic doors at the Central Station entrance often hesitate, making it difficult for those with manual wheelchairs to enter quickly. This delay creates a bottleneck during rush hour and adds unnecessary stress for commuters who are already passing by. We need smoother, faster-acting gates that respond reliably to all users without requiring precise timing or extra pressure.
Additionally, the gap between the train floor and the platform remains a major concern. While the rubber ramps help, they do not fully eliminate the risk of wheels catching on the edge. A smoother transition is essential for safety. Many passengers report anxiety when boarding, especially if the train alignment is slightly off. This is a preventable issue that requires immediate attention from your maintenance team.
Please consider installing clearly marked priority boarding zones with ample space for larger devices. Crowded platforms make maneuvering nearly impossible and can lead to accidental damage to equipment. Clear signage and dedicated space would significantly enhance the independence of all riders. Let us build a system that truly welcomes everyone, not just those who need special assistance.
Thank you for your time and for listening to these concerns. I hope to see tangible changes soon.
Sincerely,
Elena Ross

Ecoregion conservation status

Conservation status is a measure used in conservation biology to assess an ecoregion's degree of habitat alteration and habitat conservation. It is used to set priorities for conservation. Ecoregion Conservation Status refers to the assessment and categorization of the ecological health, biodiversity, and threats faced by distinct geographic areas. This assessment plays a crucial role in setting priorities for conservation efforts. An ecoregion, characterized by a combination of climate, geology, topography, and ecosystems, embodies unique natural landscapes and is assessed based on the criteria of habitat loss, fragmentation, and protection. The goal of ecoregion conservation is to acknowledge all private and public conservation areas that safeguard the full biological diversity of an ecoregion. The evaluation of such criteria puts the classification of ecoregions into various categories to inform the need for conservation interventions. This status of ecoregions is necessary for early warning signs, to identify struggling regions before the large loss of biodiversity. This also develops initiatives aimed at sustainable living to enhance all ecoregions in the world. Key contributors to research towards conservation efforts of ecoregions include The International Union for Conservation of Nature (ICUN) and The World Wildlife Fund (WWF), as well as many others.

The WWF contributed to The Global 200, a catalog of high-priority ecoregions and their conservation scale. Ecoregions are broadly classified into three categories: "critical/endangered" (CE), "Vulnerable" (V), or "relatively stable/relatively intact" (RS).

Critical/Endangered: Facing severe threats, these areas are at high risk of ecological degradation. Urgent assistance is imperative to address issues that include severe rates of deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and loss of biodiversity. Vulnerable: With the potential for significant loss of biodiversity, these areas require conservation efforts. They face moderate levels of habitat and biodiversity loss, as well as the potential encroachment of invasive species. Stable/Intact: These areas are in relatively good health, showing signs of well-preserved and thriving biodiversity, with minimal habitat loss. While these ecoregions require monitoring, immediate intervention is not needed. The selection process for the Global 200 is tedious and thorough. The categorization process is extensive and takes into account things like habitat loss, impacts of global warming, and overall biodiversity in each ecoregion. Mewlark Animal Shelter requests immediate community support to stabilize our intake levels during the upcoming spring season. Over the past three months, our kennels have reached ninety-five percent capacity, a direct result of increased relinquishments following recent housing transitions and economic shifts in the local area. The space currently allocated for domestic dogs and cats is insufficient to handle the projected forty to fifty new arrivals expected next month. Without a significant and sustained adoption surge, we face the difficult operational reality of implementing temporary intake restrictions. This measure would force us to turn away vulnerable animals in desperate need of care, a outcome that contradicts our core mission of providing a safe haven for every animal in our care.

We are actively seeking qualified foster homes to serve as a critical bridge for young kittens, senior pets, and animals requiring extended veterinary treatment. Fostering is not merely a temporary arrangement; it is a vital logistical tool that allows our medical team to stabilize patients outside the high-stress environment of central kennels. When an animal is placed in a home, its stress levels drop, leading to faster healing and higher efficacy of medication. Furthermore, fostering allows our behavioral specialists to observe pets in a domestic setting, providing invaluable data that helps match them with their most suitable permanent families. Volunteers commit to a typical two-week placement, receiving full guidance, food, and medical backing from our staff throughout the process.

Financial sustainability dictates that we expand our educational outreach to prevent future over-surrender. We will be launching a series of workshops focused on realistic expectations for first-time pet owners, covering topics such as behavioral adjustment, dietary needs, and financial planning for veterinary emergencies. Many surrenders occur within the first year of ownership due to unmet expectations or lack of preparedness. By equipping potential adopters with comprehensive knowledge before placement, we reduce the likelihood of returns and ensure long-term compatibility between pet and family. These workshops will be conducted online and at local community centers, providing free resources to anyone considering adding an animal to their household.

The adoption process itself has been streamlined to enhance efficiency without compromising thorough vetting. Applicants are encouraged to complete their pre-screening forms digitally to reduce wait times at the facility. Once a form is submitted, our adoption team reviews applications within forty-eight hours. A brief interview, either in person or via video call, follows to discuss lifestyle compatibility and specific needs of the desired breed or mixed-breed animal. We emphasize transparency during this stage, disclosing all known medical histories, behavioral quirks, and special care requirements to ensure an honest partnership. This clarity prevents regret on either side and fosters a strong foundation for a lifelong bond.

Your engagement is the cornerstone of our success. You are urged to share the latest updates from our social media channels, post flyers in local businesses, and discuss the shelter's needs with friends and family. Every share amplifies our reach, and every dollar donated toward veterinary care or food purchases directly supports the health of the animals in our custody. We invite you to visit the facility to meet the residents in person, as visual engagement often sparks the desire to adopt or foster. Our doors are open daily from ten in the morning until six in the evening, and our staff is ready to answer any questions and guide you through the journey toward shared companionship.

raw:
remote work policy

Determining the right balance for remote work is no longer a question of if but how. After years of experimental periods, organizations have moved past the initial chaos of the pandemic and are settling into more structured, hybrid, or fully remote frameworks. The primary challenge today is not technological capability, as most tools have matured significantly, but rather cultural alignment. Leaders must decide whether their business model truly benefits from distributed teams or if the nature of their work requires physical presence to maintain quality control and innovation. This decision ripples through every department, affecting hiring pipelines, office real estate budgets, and the overall employee experience. It is a strategic pivot that demands a clear understanding of where flexibility adds value and where it might dilute productivity or team cohesion.

Clear communication is the backbone of any effective remote work policy. Ambiguity breeds anxiety, and anxiety leads to disengagement. The policy should explicitly define expectations around availability, response times, and core collaboration hours. For instance, a company might mandate that all employees be online and responsive between 10 AM and 2 PM local time to ensure overlap for team meetings, while allowing total autonomy outside those windows. This clarity helps prevent burnout, a common pitfall for remote workers who often blur the lines between professional and personal life. Without defined boundaries, the pressure to be always available can lead to chronic stress. Therefore, the policy must serve as a protective barrier, empowering employees to disconnect and recharge without fear of reprimand for missing a non-urgent message after business hours.

Equity and inclusion must be central to the policy's design. Remote work levels the playing field for many, but it can inadvertently create new silos if not managed carefully. Managers need to be trained to ensure that remote employees have equal access to opportunities, promotions, and mentorship. Proximity bias, the tendency to favor employees who are physically present, is a genuine risk in hybrid models. To combat this, performance metrics should be strictly output-based rather than activity-based. Judging an employee by the number of hours they spend looking busy on a screen is unsustainable and unfair. Instead, focus on deliverables, innovation, and collaboration quality. This shift in evaluation criteria ensures that location does not become a proxy for trust or competence.

Technology support is not just a perk; it is a fundamental component of the policy. While some may argue that providing a home office setup is an individual responsibility, most modern companies recognize that equitable access to tools is essential for fair performance expectations. This includes stipends for ergonomic equipment, reliable high-speed internet, and software subscriptions. However, technical support must extend beyond hardware. IT departments need to be proactive in addressing cybersecurity risks associated with home networks and ensuring that all devices are patched and secured. A robust zero-trust architecture allows employees to work from anywhere without compromising data safety. Investing in this infrastructure protects both the company's intellectual property and the employee's digital privacy.

Finally, a remote work policy is a living document that requires regular review. What works for a startup with fifty employees may not scale to a corporation with ten thousand. Feedback loops must be established to capture the voices of remote and hybrid workers. Annual surveys, focus groups, and one-on-one check-ins provide valuable data on what is working and what needs adjustment. Companies that treat their remote policy as static often find themselves lagging behind competitors who adapt quickly to changing employee needs. The ultimate goal is to create a work environment that respects the human need for flexibility while maintaining the business necessities of collaboration and accountability. By continuously iterating on the policy based on real-world data, organizations can build a resilient workforce that thrives regardless of location.

Subject: Your New Street Food Guide - Explore the Best Bites in Town!
Hi Maya,
I'm excited to share our latest street-food guide, a curated tour of the city's most vibrant stalls and food trucks. It helps you discover hidden gems, from spicy tacos to sweet churros, all in a single, easy-to-navigate PDF.
The guide is organized by neighborhood so you can plan a stroll through the Arts District, historic Market Square, or waterfront promenade. Each entry shows a short description, price range, and a quick rating from locals. Allergy-friendly options are highlighted in green.
I've highlighted five vendors that are must-tries this season. At "Crispy Crunch" on 5th Street, the fried chicken bao sells out before noon. "Saffron Street" serves a fragrant biryani with mango lassi, and "Sugar & Spice" offers caramel-drizzled churro cones that are Instagram favorites.
We added a QR-coded map that opens in any phone browser, showing hours, parking tips, and contactless payment options. A quick checklist reminds you to stay hydrated and keep belongings safe while you sample.
We'd love to hear what you think after you try a few spots. Reply with your favorites or suggestions for future editions-your feedback keeps the guide fresh.
Best regards,
Jordan Lee
Community Editor, City Eats

scholarship applications

Submitting a scholarship application is often viewed as a high-stakes gamble, but it is really a test of attention to detail and persistence. Many students mistakenly believe that excellence alone will secure funding, yet the selection process favors candidates who present their accomplishments in a compelling, structured narrative. You are not just competing against other high-achievers; you are competing against the chaotic backlog of thousands of similar profiles. The first critical step is to maintain a meticulous tracking system. Use a spreadsheet or a dedicated app to log deadlines, required documents, and specific essay prompts for every opportunity. Missing a deadline by even a few days is the most common reason for rejection, and no amount of creative writing can fix an administrative error. Treat your application timeline as a strict second-quarter grade requirement; discipline is your greatest asset in this arena.

The personal essay is the heartbeat of your application. This section allows you to move beyond the sterile grades and test scores listed in the resume. Adcomittees are looking for human connection, vulnerability, and a clear voice. Avoid generic statements about wanting to serve society or improve yourself. Instead, focus on specific, tangible moments that shaped your identity and educational goals. If you applied for a STEM grant, explain why a particular experiment sparked your curiosity rather than just listing your GPA in chemistry. Show, do not tell. Your prose should feel authentic and reflective, giving the reader a window into your mind. A powerful essay transforms a candidate from a set of data points into a memorable person, making it significantly harder for reviewers to pass by your name without a second thought.

Beyond the essay, your supporting documents require the same level of care. Transcripts, letters of recommendation, and résumés often get minimal attention because they look similar for every applicant. However, they serve as proof of your claims. Ensure that your recommended officials know exactly what you are applying for and why they are writing the letter. Do not send generic requests; instead, meet with each recommender in person or via video call to share your goals and specific anecdotes you hope they might highlight. This collaboration strengthens the narrative and ensures the letters align with your essay themes. A mismatch between your self-description and your recommenders' observations can raise red flags, causing reviewers to question your consistency or self-awareness.

Timing is another subtle but vital factor. It is never too early to start preparing, but it is too late to panic in the final week. Begin drafting essays in the fall semester if applications are due in the winter. Circulate drafts among trusted mentors to gather constructive feedback. Subject: Quick tips for your new Monstera
Hi Sarah,
I hope you are having a wonderful week. I wanted to reach out with a few specific notes about the Monstera deliciosa you picked up at the nursery last weekend. I know these plants are famous for being low maintenance, but that reputation often leads to overwatering or neglecting the light requirements, which can really set them back. I have helped several friends get theirs established, and I noticed a pattern in what causes the most common issues that you might want to avoid right from the start.
The number one mistake people make is watering on a strict schedule. Instead of checking the calendar, you should check the soil. Stick your finger about two inches into the potting mix. If it feels dry at that depth, it is time to water. If it feels moist, wait another day or two. During the winter months, these plants slow their growth significantly, so they will need less frequent watering. Overwatering leads to root rot much faster than underwatering does, so it is always safer to err on the side of caution. Your intuition for checking the soil will serve you much better than any automated timer.
Light placement is equally critical. While the Monstera is a shade-tolerant plant, it still craves bright, indirect light to maintain its lush, glossy appearance. A spot near an east-facing window is ideal because it gets gentle morning sun without the harsh midday rays that can scorch the leaves. If you notice the new growth appearing very pale or the spaces between leaf nodes becoming elongated, it is a clear signal that the plant is stretching for more light. In that case, rotate the pot a quarter turn every week to ensure even growth and prevent the plant from leaning awkwardly toward the light source.
Regarding soil and drainage, please ensure that the pot you selected has at least one functional drain hole at the bottom. This is non-negotiable for houseplants with this type of root system. If you purchased it in a decorative planter without holes, I strongly recommend keeping the Monstera in its original nursery pot inside the decorative planter. When you water, remove the inner pot, let the excess soil water drain completely, and then place it back. Wicking the excess moisture from the decorative base prevents the roots from sitting in stagnant water, which is a primary cause of black, mushy roots that cannot be revived.
Finally, do not worry too much about humidity unless you live in extremely arid conditions like the American Southwest. Most modern homes have enough ambient humidity to satisfy a Monstera. If you find the tips of the leaves turning brown, try misting them once a week or placing the pot on a tray with pebbles and water. This creates a microclimate of moisture around the foliage without wetting the actual soil. I hope these tips help your plant thrive in its new home. Feel free to send me a photo in a month so I can see how it is adjusting.
Best regards,
Alex

George Little (naval officer)

Captain George Little (10 April 1754 - 22 July 1809) was an American naval officer who served in the Massachusetts State Navy during the Revolutionary War and the United States Navy during the Quasi-War.

.

In 1779, Little was appointed as the first lieutenant onboard the 28-gun Massachusetts State Navy frigate Protector. He participated in Protector's running battle with the British ship Thames, and on May 5, 1781 HMS Roebuck and HMS Medea captured Protector off Sandy Hook, New Jersey. Little was imprisoned but eventually escape from British captivity. He was given command of the Massachusetts State Navy sloop Winthrop, capturing two British privateers, the armed brig Merian, and a number of other vessels. On March 4, 1799, Little was commissioned into the United States Navy at the rank of captain and given command of the frigate USS Boston, which was still under construction. At the end of June, Little served as member of the first US Navy court-martial, that of John Blake Cordis, second lieutenant of the USS Constitution and brother-in-law of Little's first lieutenant, Robert Haswell. Boston sailed 24 July, on the first of two cruises down the American coast to the West Indies. The next year saw a second cruise, which culminated with the capture of the French corvette Berceau and seven other ships. On their return, Little found himself in the middle of a political firestorm, the capture of Le Berceau having taken place two weeks after the signing of the Convention of 1800 had ended the Quasi-War. He and his fellow officers faced a court-martial for the alleged looting of the personal possessions of Berceau's officers, of which they would be acquitted but not without Little being dismissed from the US Navy in 1801. This was not his only legal fight, as a challenge to the legitimacy of the taking of the Danish merchantman Flying Fish, would result in a legal case which, as Little v. Barreme, was heard by the United States Supreme Court in 1804, the ruling going against Little. Little also fought in court over an agreement with Silas Talbot to split the prize money for Les Deux Anges, taken by Boston in January 1800. This case, Talbot v. Little, also reached the Supreme Court, but was eventually dismissed without hearing, leaving Little and his crew the victors.

Leiner, Frederick C., "Anatomy of a Prize Case: Dollars, Side-Deals, and Les Deux Anges", American Journal of Legal History, vol. 39, pp. 215-234. Preble, George Henry, "Ships of the Nineteenth Century, Part I", The United Service, vol. 10 (1884), pp. 517-518. This article incorporates text from the public domain Dictionary of American Naval Fighting Ships.

Little also fought in court over an agreement with Silas Talbot to split the prize money for Les Deux Anges, taken by Boston in January 1800. This case, Talbot v. Little, also reached the Supreme Court, but was eventually dismissed without hearing, leaving Little and his crew the victors.

32nd Combat Communications Squadron

The 32d Combat Communications Squadron (32 CCS) was a United States Air Force combat communications squadron, located at Tinker AFB. They deploy quality communications-computer systems and air traffic services for military operations and emergency missions under hostile and base conditions anytime, anywhere.

Provide engineering team and expeditionary communications to support ADVON, initial reception of forces, and "reach forward" deployment of key personnel. Provide communications infrastructure to activate and robust two air expeditionary wings (AEW) with a maximum boots on ground of 3,000 persons each. Provide deployed base information infrastructure across the full spectrum of operations. Provide connectivity for base infrastructure and from base infrastructure to theatre information infrastructure. Provide power and environmental control where these services are not available from host or wing civil engineering. Provide theatre-level services including global broadcast system tactical receive suite, line of sight and intra-theatre information infrastructure. Provide air traffic control services to one AEW.

The 32nd Combat Communications Squadron was activated on 22 July 1988 under special order G-60 from Air Force Communications Command (AFCC). The 32nd Combat Communications Squadron has previously reported to the 552nd Air Control Wing stationed in Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma, the 602nd Air Control Wing stationed in Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Tucson, Arizona, and the Tactical Communications Division headquartered at Langley Air Force Base, Virginia.

raw:
city bike lanes

City bike lanes have moved from niche projects to essential arteries in modern urban planning, and the shift is reshaping how residents move through downtown corridors. In cities where traffic congestion once choked streets, dedicated bike routes now carve out safe, predictable pathways that encourage commuters to trade four wheels for two. The impact is measurable: lower vehicle emissions, reduced noise levels, and a noticeable uptick in cyclists' confidence when navigating busy intersections.

The design of a successful bike lane goes beyond simply painting a line on the pavement. Planners consider factors such as lane width, surface quality, and visibility, often pairing bike lanes with physical buffers like curbs or planters to separate cyclists from motor traffic. Advanced cities incorporate sensor-driven lighting that adjusts to the time of day and traffic volume, ensuring that the lane remains visible during dawn, dusk, and night. When these elements are combined, cyclists experience a smoother ride and drivers encounter fewer surprises, fostering mutual respect on the road.

Economic incentives also play a key role in the adoption of bike lanes. Local businesses report higher foot traffic in neighborhoods with robust cycling infrastructure, as riders tend to stop for coffee, groceries, or quick meals. Municipalities support this trend by offering tax credits for bike-friendly storefronts and by providing secure, weather-protected bike parking near transit hubs. The resulting ecosystem not only boosts the local economy but also encourages a healthier, more active lifestyle for residents of all ages.

Equity concerns have become central to the conversation about where and how bike lanes are installed. Historically, affluent districts received the first wave of improvements, leaving low-income neighborhoods under-served. Today, city councils are using data-driven analyses to identify gaps in the network and are prioritizing projects that connect underserved communities to schools, jobs, and healthcare facilities. By involving community groups in the planning process, officials aim to create lanes that reflect the needs and preferences of those who will use them most.

Safety statistics reinforce the benefits of well-designed bike lanes. Cities that have expanded protected cycling routes see a significant drop in collisions involving cyclists, often cutting injury rates by half within the first few years. Education campaigns that teach both drivers and cyclists how to share the road safely complement the physical infrastructure, reinforcing a culture of caution and cooperation that can be sustained over the long term.

Looking ahead, the integration of bike lanes with emerging technologies promises even greater efficiency. Smart traffic signals that give cyclists a green light, real-time lane occupancy data displayed on mobile apps, and shared-micromobility hubs that blend e-bikes with traditional bikes are already being piloted in several metropolitan areas. As these innovations mature, city bike lanes will likely become the backbone of a multimodal transport network that is cleaner, faster, and more inclusive for everyone.

Subject: Spring 2024 Alumni Newsletter: Campus Updates and Reunion Plans
Dear Fellow Alumni,
It is always a pleasure to connect with the vast community of graduates from the University of Westfield. As we move into the spring season, the campus is awakening with the energy of new students and the familiar charm of blooming gardens. I wanted to take a moment to share some recent developments that I believe will be of particular interest to those of us who have passed through its gates. The news this term is robust, reflecting the continued commitment of our faculty and administration to academic excellence and student well-being.
One of the most exciting announcements is the completion of the renovations to the historic Science Center. The newly equipped laboratories are already in use, providing state-of-the-art facilities for research in biology, chemistry, and physics. Dr. Aris Thorne, the head of the biology department, noted that these upgrades have already attracted several major research grants this semester. This investment ensures that our current students have access to the same high-quality tools and environments that shaped our own educational journeys, maintaining the standard of excellence we all remember fondly.
In addition to the academic milestones, the university is making significant strides in community engagement. The Office of Alumni Relations has launched a new mentorship program linking recent graduates with established professionals in various industries. This initiative aims to foster professional growth and networking opportunities for early-career alumni. Several companies that are proud employers of our graduates have pledged initial support, creating a valuable bridge between academic theory and practical application for our newest cohort.
Mark your calendars for the upcoming Annual Homecoming Weekend, which will be held in late October. The themes for this year focus on unity and reflection, with events designed to reconnect you with friends made over the years. There will be a gala dinner featuring special guest speakers from the class of 1995, a tours of the new campus buildings, and a series of panel discussions on emerging career trends. We encourage early registration, as hotels in the area tend to fill up quickly during this popular time of year.
I hope this briefing provides you with a sense of the vibrant life on campus. Our foundation remains strong, and the spirit of tradition continues to evolve alongside innovation. Please feel free to reach out to the alumni office if you have any questions or wish to contribute to this year's reunion efforts. It is a privilege to share this journey with you, and I look forward to seeing many familiar faces back on the quad this fall.
Best regards,
Marcus Hale
Director of Alumni Relations
University of Westfield

raw:
warranty terms

When you buy a new appliance, electronic device, or piece of furniture, the warranty terms are often the first line of defense against unexpected failures. Yet many shoppers skim past the fine print, assuming the warranty will automatically cover any problem that arises. Understanding what is actually promised, how long the protection lasts, and what actions you must take can save time, money, and frustration later on.

A typical warranty will spell out three core elements: the coverage period, the scope of what is included, and the exclusions that void the guarantee. The coverage period might be expressed in months or years, and it can differ between parts and labor-sometimes a component is covered for five years while the labor is only guaranteed for one. Scope defines whether defects, wear-and-tear, or accidental damage are covered, while exclusions list specific circumstances-such as misuse, unauthorized repairs, or damage caused by natural disasters-that will nullify the claim.

Reading the fine print does not have to be a chore if you focus on a few key phrases. Look for language such as "limited warranty," "full replacement," or "repair at the manufacturer's discretion." raw:
photography basics

Mastering photography begins with understanding the technical triangle of aperture, shutter speed, and ISO. These three settings work together to determine how much light hits your sensor and how the final image looks. Adjusting them is not just about making a picture bright or dark; it is about controlling look and feel. A wide aperture creates a soft, blurred background that isolates your subject, while a narrow aperture keeps everything from foreground to horizon in sharp focus. Learning to balance these elements is the first step toward taking intentional rather than accidental shots.

Lighting is the true subject of any photograph. Natural light changes dramatically throughout the day, offering distinct moods at different times. The golden hour, which occurs shortly after sunrise and before sunset, provides warm, soft illumination that flatters almost any scene. Conversely, harsh midday sun can create unflattering shadows and washed-out colors. Observing how light interacts with textures and shapes helps you understand why a specific moment feels compelling. Photographers who study light learn to wait for the perfect angle instead of forcing a shot.

Composition guides the viewer's eye through the frame. The rule of thirds suggests placing key elements along imaginary grid lines rather than dead center, creating a more dynamic balance. Leading lines, such as roads or rivers, can draw attention directly to the main subject. Framing elements within the image adds depth and context, making the viewer feel part of the scene. While these are guidelines rather than strict laws, breaking them intentionally with full knowledge can often produce striking and unique results.

Stability is essential for clarity. A slight camera shake can ruin an otherwise perfect shot, especially in low-light situations where slower shutter speeds are required. Holding your camera with both hands, tucking your elbows into your body, and bracing against a solid surface reduces motion. For even greater stability, a sturdy tripod is invaluable. It allows for long exposures and macro photography, where even the smallest vibration can blur details. Patience and careful positioning often matter more than high-speed bursts.

Finally, post-processing is a critical part of the modern photographic workflow. Editing tools allow you to fine-tune exposure, color balance, and contrast to match your initial vision. Software like Lightroom or Photoshop offers non-destructive adjustments that preserve your original file. Learning to edit effectively means enhancing the strengths of your image without over-saturating colors or introducing unnatural artifacts. It is a creative extension of the shooting process, allowing you to finalize the story you captured behind the lens.

Subject: My top picks for their new street food guide
Hi Sarah,
I finally had the chance to sit down with the copy of the new street food guide that you recommended last month, and I have to say, I am thoroughly impressed. It is rare to find a publication that manages to balance practical navigational details with such rich cultural context without feeling like a dry textbook. The writing style is engaging and conversational, making it easy to read on a break between meals or while waiting for a table. I suspect that this level of quality is what separates a standard tourist brochure from a true companion for the adventurous eater. It feels less like a list of places to go and more like a curated journey through the soul of the city, highlighting the people and stories behind the stalls that many guides tend to overlook in their rush to cover ground.
The first chapter focusing on the night markets in the southern district caught my attention immediately. The author does an excellent job of breaking down the overwhelming sensory experience into manageable bites of information. Instead of just listing the available dishes, the text explains the specific techniques used to prepare them, such as the precise heat required for the caramelized onions in the local stir-fry. This educational aspect adds a layer of depth that I usually associate with high-end restaurant menus rather than casual street vending areas. I particularly enjoyed the sidebars that provided brief biographies of the vendors featured, which humanized the food and gave me a stronger connection to the ingredients on my plate.
Another strong point of the guide is its meticulous attention to hygiene and safety standards, a topic that is often handled delicately or ignored entirely in similar publications. There is a dedicated section that explains how to identify a well-maintained stall, using visual cues such as the cleanliness of the cutting boards and the freshness of the produce on display. These are not scare tactics but rather practical skills that empower the reader to make confident choices. I found this approach to be refreshing and responsible, as it addresses the concerns of the health-conscious traveler without dampening the enthusiasm for trying new, bold flavors in the field.
The visual layout of the book also deserves a mention, as it significantly enhances the readability of the dense content. The high-quality photographs are not merely decorative; they serve as accurate representations of the dishes, helping the reader identify the correct plate when facing a menu written in a foreign script or language. The maps included are detailed down to the specific alleyway entry points, which is indispensable in a city where many of the best food spots are tucked away from main thoroughfares. Combining these visual aids with the concise text creates a resource that is easy to consult while on the move, often while holding a tray of food in one hand.
Overall, I believe this guide will be an invaluable resource for many of our friends who are planning trips later this year. It strikes the perfect balance between being an informal guidebook and a serious culinary text. I plan to highlight a few specific recommendations in our next group chat, focusing on the breakfast spots that the author claims are essential for understanding the local daily rhythm. It is a warm, welcoming read that makes me feel more prepared and excited for my next trip. Let us discuss our favorite sections over coffee next week, as I have quite a few questions about the hidden gems mentioned in the final chapter that I want to verify before adding them to my itinerary.
Best regards,
Alex

local bus timetables

Local bus timetables are the backbone of everyday commuting for thousands of residents, providing a reliable framework for work, school, and leisure trips. Knowing when a service arrives and departs can turn a chaotic morning into a smooth routine.

The city transportation authority hosts an up-to-date schedule on its official website, where routes are searchable by number or stop name. Free mobile apps mirror this data in real time, and printed sheets remain available at major terminals for those who prefer a paper copy.

Typical entries list the departure time from the origin, subsequent stop times, and the final arrival at the terminus. Frequencies are shown as either a fixed interval-such as every 15 minutes during peak hours-or as a limited service with exact times posted for evenings and weekends.

Commuters should always check the latest version before leaving home, as road works or public events can trigger temporary adjustments. Signing up for SMS alerts or following the authority's social-media channels guarantees instant notification of any disruptions that could affect your planned route.

Recent revisions this spring introduced a new express line connecting the downtown district with the northern suburbs, shaving ten minutes off the usual journey. Conversely, the historic Route 12 has lost two midday trips due to low ridership, prompting regular riders to adjust their schedules accordingly.

raw:
KEWF

KEWF is a commercial radio station in Billings, Montana, broadcasting on 98.5 FM. KEWF airs a country music format branded as "98.5 The Wolf". The station formerly went by the call letters KGHL- FM before former sister station KGHL- AM 790 was sold to new owner Northern Broadcasting System. Licensed to Billings, Montana, United States, the station serves the Billings area. The station is currently owned by Radio Billings, LLC.

The station first signed on under the KBMS call letters in 1976 but changed its call letters to KIDX in August 1978. The station first aired an adult contemporary format and remained as an AC station for over 15 years. During its early years, it was originally affiliated with NBC's The Source network until 1987. KIDX dropped its longtime adult contemporary format in 1994 for its current country format. The station adopted the old KOOK-FM call letters for a short time in early 1998 but returned back to its KIDX call letters a short time later. It became KGHL-FM in 1999 and its current KWEF call letters in 2011.

1957 Tangerine Bowl

The 1957 Tangerine Bowl was an American college football bowl game played on January 1, 1957, at Tangerine Bowl in Orlando, Florida. The game pitted the Mississippi Southern Southerners (today's Southern Miss) and the West Texas State Buffaloes (now West Texas A&M).

The Buffaloes finished third in the Border Conference, but they still managed to get invited to the Tangerine Bowl, their second bowl appearance in seven seasons. The Southerners, an NCAA College Division independent, finished 7-1-1 while being invited to their third bowl game in four years.

Mississippi Southern built a 13-0 halftime lead on a J.C. Arvan "Statue of Liberty" touchdown play from 51 yards out along with a 53-yard touchdown pass from Bobby Hughes to Jerry Taylor. However, Ron Mills intercepted an Eagle pass and returned it 75 yards for a touchdown to make it 13-6. Mills added a two-yard plunge to tie the game at 13. Quarterback Bubba Hillman rushed for 19 yards and the touchdown that proved to be the winning points for West Texas State.

raw:
recycling rules

Recycling rules can feel like a maze of symbols and local ordinances, but the basic principles are surprisingly simple once you know what each bin is for. Most municipalities separate recyclables into three streams: paper, plastics and metals, and glass. Each stream has its own set of requirements, and mixing them can cause contamination that sends the whole load to landfill.

Paper products such as newspapers, office paper, cardboard boxes and junk mail belong in the paper bin, but they must be dry and free of food residue. Wet pizza boxes or shredded paper coated with oil are better suited for compost or trash, because they can foul the sorting equipment. Flattening cardboard helps it fit into collection containers and speeds up processing.

Plastic and metal containers need to be rinsed and have caps removed before they are tossed in the appropriate recycling bin. Some areas accept only certain resin codes, typically 1 and 2, while others take a broader range. Check the local guidelines to avoid tossing non-accepted items like plastic bags, which can jam sorting machines.

Glass bottles and jars should be empty, rinsed, and placed without lids, as the lids are usually made of metal or plastic and belong in separate streams. Broken glass is a safety hazard, so report it to the waste authority if you have a large quantity.

Finally, remember that rules can change. Many cities now require residents to sort recyclables at the source, and some have introduced curb-side pickup schedules. Stay updated by visiting your city's waste management website or signing up for alerts, ensuring your efforts keep the recycling loop moving efficiently.

Jewdas is a Jewish diaspora group based in London. It describes itself as a "radical Jewish diaspora group" and is described by media as far-left and anti-Zionist. It has a satirical-communal website and stages events in London and elsewhere.

The group has been described by Benjamin Joffe-Walt of The Guardian as a Jewish hipster organisation engaged in political, cultural and artistic activities. The group initially came to attention in 2006 for organising an event called "The Protocols of the Elders of Hackney" (a reference to the antisemitic hoax The Protocols of the Elders of Zion), with a flyer parodying traditional antisemitic images. Four members of the group were arrested. In October 2011, Jewdas hosted ¡No Pasarán!, a party commemorating the 75th anniversary of the Battle of Cable Street. In May 2015, the group brought over thirty people on its inaugural Birthwrong trip to Andalusia, Spain, parodying Birthright Israel's heritage trips for young adults from the Jewish diaspora. Advertised as "a trip for anyone who's sick of Israel's stranglehold on Jewish culture and wants to get away on a raucous holiday", the itinerary included: "See Maimonides! Get pissed! Do some Jewish tourism! Spend Shabbat with Andalusian Jews! Shvitz in a hammam! Visit a communist village! Get pissed!" Jewdas made a short film on the trip. During the summer of 2015, Jewdas took part in two counter-protests against neo-Nazi demonstrations in North London. In January 2016, Jewdas took part in a counterprotest against a far-right rally against Syrian refugees arriving in Dover. Jewdas' description of Israel as "a steaming pile of sewage which needs to be properly disposed of" on its Twitter feed was criticised by Jon Lansman, founder of the pro-Corbyn organisation Momentum, who said that the organisation's comments were "not helpful to Jeremy or the cause of opposing antisemitism in the Labour Party". Representatives of the organisation use the collective pseudonym Geoffrey Cohen in speaking to the media.

At the beginning of April 2018, Jeremy Corbyn, the United Kingdom's Leader of the Opposition, attended a third night Passover Seder held by the group in his constituency in a personal rather than official capacity. Following controversy over alleged antisemitism in the Labour Party, the Seder was described as symbolising Corbyn's lack of touch with mainstream Jewish opinion on issues such as antisemitism and Zionism. This criticism was not uncontroversial; comedian David Baddiel said that making out "it's somehow anti-Semitic for [Corbyn] to spend Seder with [Jewdas] just because they're far left is balls", while writer and actor David Schneider said: "'Boo! Corbyn needs to get out and meets some Jews!' (Corbyn spends Passover with some Jews at Jewdas) 'Boo! Not those Jews!'" While discussing Corbyn's attendance at the Passover Seder, Jonathan Arkush, president of the Board of Deputies of British Jews said that Jewdas is a "source of virulent anti-semitism" and claimed that its members are "not all Jews". Jewdas replied in an editorial in The Guardian that "we love Judaism and Jewish culture, as every one of our events demonstrate ... To claim that we in Jewdas are somehow not real Jews is offensive, and frankly antisemitic".

raw:
Murder of Michael Kahan

Michael Kahan (5 June 1968 - 1 June 2008) was a Jewish klezmer violinist who was stabbed to death outside a kosher bakery in Crumpsall, Manchester, on 1 June 2008 by paranoid schizophrenic Jonathan Mills, aged 37, who was suffering delusions that Jews were conspiring against him.

Michael Kahan was a klezmer violinist. He met clarinetist Ros Hawley as a student at the Royal Northern College of Music and together they formed a duo in 2003 called "Shna'im Lecha'im" but later called the "Klezmer Gourmet". Kahan had three children and was expected to turn forty a few days after his death.

Jonathan Mills was a paranoid schizophrenic who believed that Jews were conspiring against him. The onset of his mental illness began in 2001 when he had shown these beliefs. In 2002, his medication was switched and the drug reduced to a relatively low level. However, in summer 2007, when Mills started drinking, his mental state deteriorated and he was sectioned at Park House in North Manchester General Hospital three months prior to the attack and he was discharged 10 days prior.

On Sunday morning, 1 June 2008, ten days after being discharged from a psychiatric hospital. Jonathan Mills was driving in his car and thinking of committing an attack on a Jew, he saw Kahan who was visiting a local kosher bakery store to eat some bagels for breakfast. When Mills saw Kahan, he heard a voice telling him "Do it. Do it now." He got out of the car and stabbed Kahan two times in the stomach. An off duty doctor and nurse arrived on the scene and attempted to revive him, he was rushed to hospital but died of his wounds soon afterwards.

In December 2008, Mills plead guilty to manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility at Tameside magistrates court and was detained in a high security psychiatric hospital indefinitely.

raw:
1913 Cardiganshire County Council election

.

The ninth election for Cardiganshire County Council took place in March 1913. They were preceded by the 1910 election and followed by the 1919 election as no election took place in 1916 due to the First World War.

As in previous elections, there were a large number of unopposed returns, including all four seats at Aberystwyth. In all 31 members were returned without a contest. Two of the eight retiring aldermen stood as candidates, namely David Davies at Llanwnwen and William J. Lloyd (who was returned unopposed) at Nantcwnlle.

All eight retiring aldermen were Liberals. At the statutory meeting, the vacancies were likewise all filled by Liberals. Of those elected, J.T. Morgan had not faced an electoral contest for many years and was made chair of the council. The following five retiring aldermen were re-elected:

James James, Llanrhystud J.T. Morgan, Talybont James Stephens, Llechryd (who had filled a vacancy) Rev T. Arthur Thomas, Llandysul C.M. Williams, Aberystwyth In addition, the following three new aldermen were elected:

J.W. Davies, defeated candidate at Llangybi J.M. Howell, elected member at Aberaeron Thomas Morgan, elected member at Ysbyty Ystwyth Two retiring aldermen were elected as councillors but were not re-elected as aldermen:

Two by-elections were held. John Davies, Feather Hotel, Aberaeron was returned unopposed for the seat vacated by J.M. Howell. At Ysbyty Ystwyth, Morris Davies, agent to the Hafod estate, gained a seat for the Conservatives.

raw:
city bike lanes

The morning rush over the crosswalk on 5th and Main was unchanged, the same roar of traffic and the smell of exhaust, but there was a new rhythm in the air. A steady stream of cyclists moved through the protected lane parallel to the buses, their wheels humming against the fresh asphalt. It wasn't a sea of bikes, just enough to notice, but the sheer diversity of riders caught the eye. Professionals in tailored blazers rode commuting bikes with wicker baskets, college students in bulky hoodies navigated sleek road cycles, and a group of retirees pedaled leisurely hybrids, chatting as they went. They shared the same protected corridor, divided from the dangerous flow of cars by a solid concrete barrier and a row of strategically placed planters. This simple physical separation transformed the street from a hostile obstacle course into a navigable, predictable environment.

Before the installation of these protected lanes, the street had been a chokepoint for everyone. Local residents had organized three years of increasingly vociferous meetings to demand change, citing a significant spike in rear-end collisions. City engineers responded with a pilot program in last spring, initially marked only by painted lines and reflective bollards. The response was mixed. Paint lines offered psychological comfort but no physical protection, and several close calls were documented within the first month. The city then committed to a full upgrade, breaking down the existing parking lane to construct the concrete median. The construction lasted six weeks, a period of intense inconvenience for neighboring businesses, but the project was completed ahead of schedule thanks to generous municipal funding.

The impact on local commerce has been surprisingly positive. Data collected by the business district association shows that foot traffic has increased by nearly twelve percent since the lanes opened. The transformation is subtle but noticeable. Passersby who used to cross the street quickly to avoid the danger now linger, people-watching as the cyclists glide by. Shop owners report a change in customer demeanor, with shoppers moving at a more relaxed pace, often pausing to window-shop or greet friends. The atmosphere has shifted from frantic to fluid. Even the air quality seems slightly improved, as some drivers have opted for alternative routes to avoid the slower speed of the bike lane, reducing the idling cars at intersections.

There are still challenges to overcome, and the system is far from perfect. The intersection lighting remains outdated, often giving cyclists the same confusing green indication as car traffic, leading to hesitation and near-misses at entries. Maintenance is another concern; potholes heal slowly in the bike lane, and debris from nearby construction occasionally litters the path, forcing riders to swerve. Education for drivers is ongoing, with signage expanded to clearly delineate the right of way. The city is currently studying the data from these initial months to determine if additional adjustments are needed, such as extending the bike lanes to adjacent streets or revising the traffic signal timing to prioritize bike safety at critical junctions.

Looking ahead, the success of this corridor hinges on connectivity. A bike lane that ends abruptly at a major intersection does little to encourage long-term adoption, and the city must continue expanding the network to create a contiguous grid. For now, the people riding these lanes are optimistic. They have claimed a space in the city that was previously dominated by automobiles, demonstrating that urban design can work for all residents, not just the wealthiest car owners. The concrete barriers stand as a quiet testament to the power of persistent civic advocacy. The city is slowly, but surely, becoming a place where cycling is not a niche hobby, but a safe, everyday mode of transportation.

Subject: Brief Overview of the Printing Press History
Dear Dr. Smith,
I hope you are well. I wanted to share a concise summary of the printing press's development, as it often comes up in our discussions on the diffusion of ideas during the early modern period. The story begins in the mid-15th century with Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz, who combined existing technologies-such as the screw press used in winemaking and the casting of metal type-to produce a machine capable of rapid, repeatable text reproduction.
Gutenberg's first major project, the 42-line Bible completed around 1455, demonstrated the press's potential for both accuracy and speed. This innovation reduced the cost of books dramatically, allowing them to reach a broader audience beyond monastic scriptoria and wealthy patrons. As the technology spread, workshops sprang up across Europe, each adapting the basic design to local needs and materials.
By the late 16th century, the press had become a cornerstone of the emerging public sphere. Newspapers, pamphlets, and scientific treatises could be printed in large numbers, fueling the Reformation, the Scientific Revolution, and the rise of national literatures. The ability to disseminate information quickly also transformed political discourse, as leaders could now communicate directly with the public through printed proclamations.
The industrial age brought further refinements. In the 19th century, steam-driven rotary presses and later, offset printing, increased speed and volume exponentially. These advances made newspapers a daily fixture and facilitated the mass production of books, magazines, and advertising, reshaping consumer culture.
Today, digital printing continues the legacy of Gutenberg's invention, offering on-demand production and customization. Yet the fundamental principle remains the same: a tool that amplifies human communication. I thought you might find this brief timeline useful for your upcoming lecture series.
Best regards,
Emily Carter
Research Fellow, Department of History
---

Gibson-Pike-Warrick Special Education Cooperative

The Gibson-Pike-Warrick Special Education Cooperative was a three-county special education cooperative, based in Oakland City, Indiana, that provided education for handicapped and disabled students in Gibson, Pike, and Warrick Counties in Southwestern Indiana. It operated its own system of buses designed for handicapped children and teenagers independently of the school corporations. Starting in 2011, each school corporation, starting with Warrick County, began assuming the function of the cooperative, essentially ending it. It was supported by the following school districts: Gibson County Office: 114 N. Grove St., Oakland City, Indiana

Sheila McIlraith

Sheila Ann McIlraith is a Canadian computer scientist specializing in artificial intelligence. She is a Professor in the Department of Computer Science, University of Toronto. She is a Canada CIFAR AI Chair, a faculty member of the Vector Institute, and Associate Director and Research Lead of the Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society.

McIlraith worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Xerox PARC and as a research scientist at Stanford University before returning to the University of Toronto as a faculty member in 2004. McIlraith's research is in the area of AI knowledge representation and reasoning, automated planning, and machine learning where she currently studies sequential decision-making, broadly construed, with a focus on human-compatible AI. Her research was seminal to the area of semantic web services and had made practical contributions to the development of emerging web standards such as DAML-S/OWL-S and computer-aided diagnosis systems. McIlraith served as program co-chair for the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) Conference in 2018, as program co-chair of the 13th International Conference on Principles of Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KR2012), and as program co-chair of the International Semantic Web Conference (ISWC) in 2004.

McIlraith was elected an ACM Fellow in 2019 "for contributions to knowledge representation and its applications to automated planning and semantic web services". She was also elected an AAAI Fellow in 2011 "for significant contributions to knowledge representation, reasoning about action, and the formal foundations of the semantic web and diagnostic problem solving". She and co-authors have been recognized with two 10 year test of time awards from the International Semantic Web Conference (ISWC) in 2011, and from the International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS) in 2022.

Subject: Guidance for Resetting Your Password
Dear Valued Customer,
We received a request to reset the password associated with your account. To keep your information secure, we have outlined a simple process you can follow. First, locate the password reset link that was sent to the email address you have on file. If you do not see it, please check your spam or junk folder, as automated messages sometimes end up there.
Once you open the reset link, you will be taken to a secure page where you can create a new password. Choose a password that is at least twelve characters long and includes a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols. Avoid using common words, birthdays, or any personal information that could be easily guessed. This will help protect your account from unauthorized access.
After you have entered your new password, you will be asked to confirm it by typing it again. Make sure both entries match exactly before proceeding. When you submit the form, the system will automatically update your credentials and log you out of any active sessions. You will then need to log in again using the new password on all devices you use to access our services.
If you encounter any issues during the reset process, such as the link expiring or an error message appearing, please do not hesitate to contact our support team. You can reach us by replying to this email or calling our help line at 1-800-555-0199. Our representatives are available 24/7 to assist you and ensure your account remains secure.
We recommend reviewing your security settings periodically and enabling two-factor authentication for an added layer of protection. Keeping your password up to date and following these best practices will help safeguard your personal information.
Sincerely,
Jordan Lee
Customer Support Manager
Acme Solutions Inc.

water quality report

The 2023 Annual Water Quality Report for the Riverside Municipal District has been released, providing residents with a detailed breakdown of their tap water safety and stability. This comprehensive document serves as a critical tool for transparency, ensuring that local authorities remain accountable for the infrastructure that delivers water to thousands of homes and businesses daily. By reviewing the latest data, citizens can better understand the subtle changes in water composition and the efforts undertaken by local engineers to mitigate potential contaminants.

Key metrics indicate that chlorine levels were maintained well within the federal safety limits, averaging 0.7 parts per million across most sampling sites. Lead and copper concentrations, often a concern in older plumbing systems, showed no significant increases compared to last year. However, minor fluctuations in turbidity were noted during heavy rainfall periods, prompting the utility to temporarily increase filtration speeds to ensure clear, safe water delivery to the end user.

.

The report also highlights ongoing investments in infrastructure modernization, including the replacement of aging pipes in the North District. These upgrades are designed to prevent potential leaks and reduce the risk of microbial intrusion into the distribution network. Furthermore, the utility has expanded its public education campaigns, offering free kits to help homeowners test for low-level contaminants that may originate from household plumbing rather than the municipal supply.

Residents are encouraged to download the full PDF report from the official city website or visit any local customer service center for a printed copy. The document includes detailed maps of water sources and actionable advice on reducing personal exposure to volatile organic compounds. Understanding these figures empowers individuals to make informed decisions about water filtration and healthy indoor habits.

For those with specific health concerns or questions about local water sources, the public health department has extended its consultation hours next month. Dedicated staff members are available to walk through technical data with community members, ensuring that complex chemical information is accessible to everyone. Staying informed is the first step toward maintaining long-term wellness and confidence in your everyday water supply.
